options: Significant labour legislation and major economic policy are negotiated there BEFORE Parliament — social dialogue seeking consensus rather than imposition

economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.subject: economics
economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.question: NEDLAC's honest limitation is:
options: It meets only once a decade
Consensus-seeking is slow, and constituencies that are not well organised are less well represented at the table

economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.subject: economics
economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.question: The consistent macro-economic aims are:
options: Performance (growth), employment creation, equitable distribution, economic stability and external stability

economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.subject: economics
economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.question: The permanent tension between the aims is that:
options: Redistribution needs revenue which needs growth; growth may need incentives favouring the advantaged; stability constrains borrowing for social spending

economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.subject: economics
economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.question: Measurable achievements of redress include:
options: Expanded access to basic services, housing, education and grants; a substantial Black middle and professional class; shifted ownership and management demographics; and a body of protective law

economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.subject: economics
economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.question: The critique that "broad-based" in B-BBEE responds to is:
options: That benefits sometimes concentrated among a narrow elite rather than spreading broadly

economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.subject: economics
economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.question: The two matric candidates illustrate that:
options: Same exam and same effort can meet very different starting lines

economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.subject: economics
economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.question: The starting lines came from:
options: LAWS deciding who could own land, where families could live, which schools got money, and who could hold which job

economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.subject: economics
economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.question: "The law is equal now" and "the economy is equal now" differ because:
options: Repeal stopped the machine but did not undo what it built — transferred land, lost schooling and absent collateral persist
Equality is purely a legal concept

economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.subject: economics
economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.question: "Land alone is a field, not a farm" means:
options: Without seed money, equipment, training and buyers, a title deed feeds nobody — transfer PLUS support, or the transfer fails

economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.subject: economics
economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.question: Skills redress is funded and delivered through:
options: A skills levy funding learnerships, apprenticeships and trade training — building qualifications people were denied

economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.subject: economics
economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.question: "Just start a business" is easy advice for someone with capital, contacts and a customer list, which is why entrepreneurship redress provides:
options: Incubators, simpler paperwork, procurement set-asides and mentorship

economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.subject: economics
economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.question: The one test to apply to any redress instrument:
options: Does it hand over a THING, or does it build a working LIVELIHOOD?
Does it cost less than last year?
Was it copied from another country?

economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.subject: economics
economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.question: A notice inviting public comment on a proposed tariff increase is an example of:
options: Public participation — regulators and lawmakers required to hear those affected before deciding

economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.subject: economics
economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.question: NEDLAC is "deliberately slower than one minister deciding" because:
options: The people who will live with a policy argue about it before it becomes law — consensus over imposition

economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.subject: economics
economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.question: Self-regulating bodies such as professional councils:
options: Set and police professional standards INSIDE a legal framework — decisions devolved to those who understand the work, with public accountability

economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.subject: economics
economics.grade10.economic-redress-and-d.question: The fair way to judge redress is:
options: BOTH columns — real gains in services, housing, schooling, grants and a growing professional class; real shortfalls in unemployment, inequality, land reform pace and narrowly pooled benefits
Neither — the question is purely political

economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.subject: economics
economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.question: Self-sufficiency's brutal constraint was:
options: You consume only what you yourself can make — every skill in every household, nothing done particularly well

economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.subject: economics
economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.question: Surplus is "the hinge of all economic history" because:
options: It releases people from food production — specialists emerge, and specialists must EXCHANGE

economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.subject: economics
economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.question: The double coincidence of wants means:
options: Two people wanting the same good
Wanting twice as much as you have
Trade requires finding someone who has what you want AND wants what you have

economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.subject: economics
economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.question: Barter's four failures are:
options: Double coincidence of wants; indivisibility; no common measure of value; no store of value

economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.subject: economics
economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.question: Money's functions are:
options: Medium of exchange, unit of account, store of value — with divisibility making any purchase size work

economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.subject: economics
economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.question: Good commodity moneys — cattle, salt, metals — were chosen for:
options: Durability, divisibility, portability and scarcity — precious metals winning on all four

economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.subject: economics
economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.question: Specialisation and markets "feed each other" because:
options: Specialists need markets to sell in and buy from — and deeper markets support finer specialisation
Both were invented by the state

economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.subject: economics
economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.question: Companies with ownership divided into shares evolved because:
options: Risk could be spread and capital gathered at scales no individual could reach

economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.subject: economics
economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.question: The state's three historic entries into markets were:
options: Involvement in trade, taxation, and financing infrastructure

economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.subject: economics
economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.question: Taxation transformed the ruler's interest because:
options: Larger economies yield larger revenues — rulers acquired a permanent stake in growth, and taxpayers in spending

economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.subject: economics
economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.question: Infrastructure is the classic case for public investment because:
options: It is expensive, benefits everyone, and repays its builder only indirectly — no single trader will build it

economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.subject: economics
economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.question: The analytical thread through all three entries:
options: Each state entry answers a market LIMITATION — term two's intervention logic, seen as history

economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.subject: economics
economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.question: Industrialisation's four components are:
options: Manufacturing, technological progress, mobilisation of energy, mechanisation

economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.subject: economics
economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.question: The mobilisation of energy was "the decisive break" because:
options: Production was unshackled from the limits of living bodies — muscle replaced by water, steam, electricity and oil

economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.subject: economics
economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.question: Industrialisation's costs included:
options: Harsh factory conditions, child labour and pollution — the violations that summoned labour law and regulation

economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.subject: economics
economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.question: South Africa's industrialisation arrived through:
options: MINING — diamonds and gold drawing railways inland and concentrating labour under the migrant system, with social costs still carried

economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.subject: economics
economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.question: Nobody in the self-sufficient village traded because:
options: Nobody had EXTRA — and doing everything meant doing nothing particularly well
Money had not been taxed yet

economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.subject: economics
economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.question: "Extra" changed everything because:
options: One family could eat without every member farming — the clever-handed son becomes the full-time potter

economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.subject: economics
economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.question: Swapping's four miseries were:
options: Slow roads, bad scales, greedy elders, wild animals
The great hunt for the exact partner; the half-goat problem; every deal a fresh argument; wealth that rots or walks off

economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.subject: economics
economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.question: "Money is half a trade, holdable" means:
options: The two halves of a swap were cut apart — sell to anyone, hold the value, buy from anyone else later
Money is worth half its face value
Only half the village used it

economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.subject: economics
economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.question: The tests every good money passes:
options: Sturdy, splittable, scarce, carryable — from cattle and salt to gold, notes and numbers on a phone

economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.subject: economics
economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.question: Strangers trading with strangers required:
options: RULES — honest scales, kept promises, an elder to judge disputes: trust made official

economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.subject: economics
economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.question: Families each owning a SHARE of a big venture meant:
options: No one person carried the whole risk — and capital could gather at new scales

economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.subject: economics
economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.question: The chief's three jobs — still the state's today — are:
options: REGULATE the trade, TAX the deals, BUILD what no trader would alone

economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.subject: economics
economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.question: After taxing began, the chief WANTED the market to grow because:
options: His income grew with it — a share of every harvest and deal

economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.subject: economics
economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.question: The machine-day's two new kinds of people were:
options: Those who OWN the machines and those who WORK them — whose arguments become labour relations

economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.subject: economics
economics.grade10.evolution-of-markets.s.question: The village's whole journey, in order:
options: Extra → specialists → money → market (roads, rules, shares) → state → machines

economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_1.subject: economics
economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_1.question: The three measuring points on the circular flow's one pipe are:
options: PRODUCTION, INCOME and SPENDING — three gauges that must in principle agree

economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_1.subject: economics
economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_1.question: GDP is defined as:
options: All money spent by government in a year
The total market value of all FINAL goods and services produced WITHIN a country's borders in a given period
The income of a country's citizens worldwide
The total of all sales including intermediate goods

economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_1.subject: economics
economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_1.question: "Market value" appears in the definition because:
options: Prices let unlike things — haircuts and coal — be added into one total

economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_1.subject: economics
economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_1.question: GDP is measured as:
options: A stockpile of everything ever produced
A FLOW per period — usually one year, reported quarterly

economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_2.subject: economics
economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_2.question: Wheat R4 → flour R7 → loaf R18. GDP counts:
options: R18 only (or the value added: 4 + 3 + 11) — intermediate goods are already inside the loaf's price

economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_2.subject: economics
economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_2.question: A foreign-owned mine on South African soil counts in:
options: SOUTH AFRICAN GDP — geography decides, not nationality

economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_2.subject: economics
economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_2.question: Uncle reselling his old bakkie is excluded because:
options: It was counted when new — reselling changes ownership without new production (though a dealer's service fee is new and counts)

economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_2.subject: economics
economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_2.question: Social grants are excluded from GDP because:
options: They are too hard to measure
They are TRANSFERS — money moved without payment for production

economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_3.subject: economics
economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_3.question: The one thing GNI changes from GDP is:
options: The rule of belonging — WHO earned the income (residents' factors, wherever producing) instead of WHERE it was produced

economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_3.subject: economics
economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_3.question: The bridge from GDP to GNI:
options: Add all exports, subtract all imports
SUBTRACT factor income paid to foreign owners; ADD factor income residents earn abroad

economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_3.subject: economics
economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_3.question: South Africa's GNI runs somewhat below its GDP because:
options: Substantial foreign ownership means more factor income LEAVES than arrives — the machine here produces more than residents keep

economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_3.subject: economics
economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_3.question: Lesotho can show GNI ABOVE GDP because:
options: Many citizens work abroad and remit wages — its people earn more than its territory produces

economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_4.subject: economics
economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_4.question: Per capita GDP is:
options: GDP divided by population — output per person, the first correction for welfare comparisons
GDP divided by the number of firms

economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_4.subject: economics
economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_4.question: Comparing GDP across years also requires:
options: Stripping out the inflation effect — a bigger number is not better if prices simply rose

economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_4.subject: economics
economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_4.question: "One billionaire and ninety-nine unemployed average out respectably" exposes GDP's silence on:
options: DISTRIBUTION — the number says nothing about who holds the income

economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_4.subject: economics
economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_4.question: "A speedometer, not a report card" means GDP:
options: Is essential for what it reads — production and growth — and silent on health, fairness, unpaid work and the environment

economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_5.subject: economics
economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_5.question: The mechanic's R300 parts and R900 repair enter the count as:
options: R900 (or the mechanic's added R600 on top of the parts' R300) — never R1 200

economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_5.subject: economics
economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_5.question: Granny's grant and uncle's bakkie resale share the feature that:
options: Money MOVED without anything new being made — the count wants only the new

economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_5.subject: economics
economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_5.question: The outsider-owned shop on the street counts in the street's GDP because:
options: It stands here, employs here, produces here — the border rule, street-sized

economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_6.subject: economics
economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_6.question: The street's daughter working in Sandton counts:
options: In GNI (she is ours; her earnings come home) but NOT in the street's GDP (her work happens there)

economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_6.subject: economics
economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_6.question: GDP measures the street as:
options: A MACHINE — how much this place, as a place, produces

economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_6.subject: economics
economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_6.question: "The machine is here, the keeping is elsewhere" describes:
options: Roughly South Africa's shape — big GDP, smaller GNI, profits of foreign-owned firms riding out

economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_6.subject: economics
economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_6.question: The real story between GDP and GNI is told by:
options: Whichever number is larger being the true one
The GAP between them — reading it reveals the economy's ownership and labour structure

economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_7.subject: economics
economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_7.question: The grandmother minding four children daily is:
options: Enormous value with no receipt — uncounted, so the official number undersells streets like ours
Counted in GDP as childcare services

economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_7.subject: economics
economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_7.question: Selling the big tree for timber makes the count:
options: Go UP — while the tree's absence appears nowhere: production that eats tomorrow looks identical to production that doesn't

economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_7.subject: economics
economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_7.question: "A street can produce more and live worse" exposes the blind spot of:
options: WELL-BEING — the count sees sales, not safety, health or learning

economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_7.subject: economics
economics.grade10.gdp-and-gni.subtopic_7.question: The balanced final reading of GDP is:
options: The number is the whole truth
The number matters — growth funds wages and clinics — AND it is a speedometer, not a report card: how fast, never how well, and never for whom

economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.subject: economics
economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.question: Labour law exists because:
options: An individual worker negotiates from weakness against an employer who can wait — the law sets floors, rules and collective weight behind the weaker side

economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.subject: economics
economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.question: The Bill of Rights guarantees workers:
options: Fair labour practices, the right to form and join unions, to organise and bargain collectively, and to strike

economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.subject: economics
economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.question: SELF-GOVERNMENT in the LRA means:
options: The parties regulate their own relationship through negotiated agreements — the state sets the framework, not the wage

economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.subject: economics
economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.question: MAJORITARIANISM means:
options: The majority of firms set conditions
The union representing the MAJORITY speaks for the workforce and gains organisational rights — one authoritative voice

economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.subject: economics
economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.question: The LRA is the Act governing:
options: ENGAGEMENT — union rights, collective bargaining, strikes and lock-outs, unfair dismissal, and the dispute machinery (CCMA, Labour Courts)

economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.subject: economics
economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.question: The BCEA sets:
options: The FLOOR beneath every job — maximum hours, overtime rules, minimum leave, notice periods, bans on child and forced labour

economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.subject: economics
economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.question: The floor-not-ceiling principle means:
options: No contract may exceed the BCEA
Parties may agree BETTER than the minimums, never worse

economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.subject: economics
economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.question: COIDA's design trade is:
options: Workers pay for their own injuries
Injured workers must sue and prove fault
Workers get compensation from an employer-funded state fund WITHOUT suing; employers gain protection from individual lawsuits

economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.subject: economics
economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.question: Collective bargaining converts:
options: Many weak individual bargains into one strong collective one — representatives negotiating wages, hours and conditions

economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.subject: economics
economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.question: Bargaining councils are:
options: Standing SECTOR-level bodies of unions and employers' organisations — whose agreements can be extended to the whole sector

economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.subject: economics
economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.question: Workplace forums are for:
options: CONSULTATION inside a single large workplace — elected by all workers, on restructuring and work methods; not wage bargaining

economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.subject: economics
economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.question: The three rooms, three conversations are:
options: Union organises and negotiates; council hosts sector negotiation; forum consults inside one workplace

economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.subject: economics
economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.question: In CONCILIATION, the commissioner:
options: Facilitates the parties' OWN settlement — chairing and probing; nothing is imposed

economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.subject: economics
economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.question: MEDIATION differs from conciliation because the intermediary:
options: Actively PROPOSES solutions — which the parties remain free to accept or refuse

economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.subject: economics
economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.question: ARBITRATION ends with:
options: An AWARD — the commissioner hears evidence and decides, binding on the parties

economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.subject: economics
economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.question: A PROTECTED strike requires:
options: Procedures followed — dispute referred, notice given — shielding strikers from dismissal for striking; unprotected strikes carry no shield

economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.subject: economics
economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.question: One worker at the manager's door carries little weight because:
options: The manager weighs one replaceable person against the queue at the gate
Workers may not speak to managers

economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.subject: economics
economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.question: The union's logic is:
options: Many weak voices braided into one strong one — the whole factory's output weighed against the demand

economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.subject: economics
economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.question: The state's role in the contest is:
options: REFEREE — writing the rules and letting the sides settle the score: self-government

economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.subject: economics
economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.question: The three rulebooks answer three days:
options: The ARGUING day (LRA), the ORDINARY day (BCEA), the WORST day (COIDA)
Strike day, court day, appeal day

economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.subject: economics
economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.question: A Saturday job offering conditions below the BCEA floor is:
options: UNLAWFUL in the offer itself — the floor is a minimum, not a menu
A matter for the bargaining council

economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.subject: economics
economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.question: Under COIDA, the injured worker:
options: Must sue the employer and prove fault
Claims from the employer-funded compensation fund — medical costs, disability support, dependants' benefits — without a court battle

economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.subject: economics
economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.question: "Name the day, and you've named the Act" is a technique for:
options: Sorting exam scenarios onto the right statute by asking WHICH bad day the scenario describes

economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.subject: economics
economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.question: The ladder's three rungs, by who decides:
options: Conciliation — the parties; mediation — the parties, with suggestions; arbitration — the COMMISSIONER, binding
All three end in binding awards
All three are decided by courts
The union decides at every rung

economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.subject: economics
economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.question: Most disputes end at conciliation because:
options: The CCMA charges for higher rungs
Most disputes are half misunderstanding — and a settlement the parties built themselves is kept willingly

economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.subject: economics
economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.question: Above the CCMA stand:
options: The LABOUR COURT and the Labour Appeal Court — reviewing awards and ruling on the law

economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.subject: economics
economics.grade10.labour-rights-and-coll.question: The whole machine in one image:
options: Rights on both sides, floors under every job, a rulebook for the contest, a fund for the injured, and a ladder turning deadlock into procedure

economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.subject: economics
economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.question: Population size changes through:
options: NATURAL GROWTH (births minus deaths) and MIGRATION (arrivals minus departures)

economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.subject: economics
economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.question: 25 births and 10 deaths per thousand gives a natural growth rate of:
options: 15 per thousand — one comma five percent a year

economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.subject: economics
economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.question: Stage two (early expanding) of the demographic cycle features:
options: Death rates FALLING (water, vaccines, food) while birth rates stay high — the gap driving rapid growth
Falling birth rates with rising deaths

economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.subject: economics
economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.question: Birth rates fall in stage three because of:
options: Urbanisation, education — especially of women — family planning, and children shifting from farm labour to school costs

economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.subject: economics
economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.question: The labour force consists of:
options: Working-age people who are EMPLOYED plus those unemployed by the strict definition — without work, available, and actively seeking

economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.subject: economics
economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.question: Discouraged work-seekers are:
options: Wanting work but no longer searching — excluded by the strict definition, counted back by the EXPANDED definition

economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.subject: economics
economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.question: The unemployment rate divides the unemployed by:
options: The LABOUR FORCE — dividing by the wrong bowl is the classic error

economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.subject: economics
economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.question: South Africa's labour force profile shows:
options: An old labour force with low youth unemployment
A YOUNG labour force with youth unemployment far above the national rate, jobs clustered in metropolitan cores, and participation suppressed by discouragement

economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.subject: economics
economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.question: Labour demand is a DERIVED demand because:
options: Firms want workers for the OUTPUT they produce — demand for builders derives from demand for buildings

economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.subject: economics
economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.question: In the labour market, the counter turns around:
options: HOUSEHOLDS supply labour, FIRMS demand it, and the WAGE is its price

economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.subject: economics
economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.question: The labour demand curve slopes downward because at higher wages:
options: Firms hire fewer workers, substitute machines, or produce less

economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.subject: economics
economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.question: The SKILLS MISMATCH means:
options: The education pipeline produces too few of what firms seek while millions offer what firms need less of — the structural heart of SA unemployment

economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.subject: economics
economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.question: "Definitions before numbers" means:
options: Quote WHICH definition a figure uses — strict against expanded can differ by millions — before interpreting it

economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.subject: economics
economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.question: Youth unemployment divides:
options: Young unemployed by the whole population
Young unemployed by the YOUNG labour force
All unemployed by the youth population

economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.subject: economics
economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.question: "Structure over headline" warns that:
options: One national rate hides concentrations — among the young, the unskilled and particular provinces — where scenario questions live

economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.subject: economics
economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.question: A comment that ANALYSES rather than describes:
options: Connects the number to its MECHANISM — through demand, supply, skills or geography

economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.subject: economics
economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.question: The street's population change equals:
options: Births minus funerals, plus who moved in minus who moved away — natural growth plus migration

economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.subject: economics
economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.question: "The clinic arrived and the street boomed" describes:
options: The second season — funerals growing rare while cradles stayed full

economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.subject: economics
economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.question: The sentence explaining the whole term is:
options: Every year a big new class finishes school and arrives at the gate looking for work — against the number of gates that open

economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.subject: economics
economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.question: Uncle S'bu — not working, applying at sites, phoning about vacancies — is:
options: On the team, benched but warming up: officially UNEMPLOYED by the strict definition

economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.subject: economics
economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.question: The matric sister at school full-time is:
options: NOT in the labour force — learners don't count on the team sheet

economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.subject: economics
economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.question: Cousin Jabu — wants work, stopped searching — is:
options: Off the strict team sheet but counted by the EXPANDED definition — the gap between the counts is thousands of real Jabus

economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.subject: economics
economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.question: Jabu's quiet exit shows up statistically in:
options: PARTICIPATION falling — discouragement hides there, not in the strict unemployment rate

economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.subject: economics
economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.question: In the labour market the sellers and buyers are:
options: FAMILIES selling hours and skills; FIRMS buying them — the wage as the meeting price
Firms selling jobs; families buying them

economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.subject: economics
economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.question: "No orders, no shifts" is the street version of:
options: DERIVED demand — the demand for labour is borrowed from the demand for goods

economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.subject: economics
economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.question: The engineers' gate and the general-labour gate show:
options: Wages set by law at both gates
The market split by SKILL — short queue and strong wages at one, long queue and pressed wages at the other

economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.subject: economics
economics.grade10.population-and-the-lab.question: "A certificate is a ticket" means:
options: Training moves a worker from the crowded gate to the short one — the ladder across the skills mismatch

economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.subject: economics
economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.question: A tax on a product shifts:
options: The SUPPLY curve LEFT and up by the tax — higher price, smaller quantity, burden shared between buyer and seller
The supply curve right and down

economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.subject: economics
economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.question: A maximum price only affects the market when it is set:
options: BELOW equilibrium — where it opens a permanent shortage with queues, rationing and black markets

economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.subject: economics
economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.question: A minimum price set above equilibrium causes:
options: A permanent SURPLUS the state must buy up, store or export at a cost to the budget

economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.subject: economics
economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.question: The honest two-sided evaluation of the minimum wage is:
options: It has no effect on the labour market
It raises the incomes of workers who keep employment, while at a wage above equilibrium the quantity of labour demanded can fall

economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.subject: economics
economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.question: The DOUBLE COINCIDENCE OF WANTS is the requirement that:
options: Each trader must find someone who HAS what they want AND WANTS what they have — barter's built-in brake
Two goods must have equal value

economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.subject: economics
economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.question: Money's four functions are:
options: Medium of exchange, unit of account, store of value, and standard of deferred payment

economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.subject: economics
economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.question: Governments entered growing markets to:
options: Issue and protect currency, enforce contracts, regulate quality, tax trade, and provide what markets will not

economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.subject: economics
economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.question: South Africa's industrial development was driven inland by:
options: The MINERAL REVOLUTION — diamonds and gold pulling railways, capital and labour to the interior

economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.subject: economics
economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.question: The labour force consists of:
options: Everyone aged 15 to 64 who is employed PLUS everyone unemployed but actively seeking work

economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.subject: economics
economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.question: The demand for labour is DERIVED demand because:
options: Hiring follows the demand for what workers PRODUCE — nobody hires for its own sake

economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.subject: economics
economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.question: The Act that sets maximum ordinary hours, leave and notice beneath every contract is:
options: The BASIC CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT ACT — the floor under every job

economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.subject: economics
economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.question: The dispute ladder at the CCMA runs:
options: CONCILIATION where a commissioner helps parties settle, then ARBITRATION where the commissioner decides, with matters of law going to the Labour Court

economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.subject: economics
economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.question: The unemployment rate divides the unemployed by:
options: The LABOUR FORCE — never by the population

economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.subject: economics
economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.question: South Africa's DOMINANT type of unemployment is:
options: STRUCTURAL — skills or locations mismatched to what employers need, cured by education, training and spatial remedies

economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.subject: economics
economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.question: Redress through the four factors of production pairs:
options: Land with restitution, redistribution and tenure; labour with equity and skills; capital with ownership, procurement and finance; entrepreneurship with small-business support

economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.subject: economics
economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.question: NEDLAC seats which four constituencies before major economic laws reach Parliament?

economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.subject: economics
economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.question: "Ceilings make queues" because pinning a price below the market level means:
options: Sellers offer LESS while buyers want MORE — and the gap becomes queues, rationing and back-door sales
Sellers offer more than buyers want

economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.subject: economics
economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.question: Brown bread and maize meal carrying no VAT while most goods carry fifteen percent is an example of:
options: The state making essentials CHEAPER on purpose so more families afford them

economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.subject: economics
economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.question: "Floors make piles" means a price pinned ABOVE the market level produces:
options: A SURPLUS somebody must buy, store or ship out

economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.subject: economics
economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.question: The "wasted morning at the river" happens because:
options: The fisherman wants a goat, not maize — the double coincidence of wants fails and the swap collapses

economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.subject: economics
economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.question: As the "go-between", money:
options: Ends the double coincidence — the fisherman takes coins and buys his goat elsewhere

economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.subject: economics
economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.question: Money as the "promise-keeper" refers to its function as:
options: A STANDARD OF DEFERRED PAYMENT — buy now, pay later becomes possible

economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.subject: economics
economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.question: In the village story, the correct order of arrivals is:
options: Surplus and barter, then money, then the chief guarding coins and promises, then the machines and factories

economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.subject: economics
economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.question: The learner in class and the grandmother at rest are:
options: OFF the team — outside the labour force, not unemployed, just not playing

economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.subject: economics
economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.question: "The employer's need is second-hand" means:
options: Hiring happens because customers are buying what those hands will make — derived demand

economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.subject: economics
economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.question: "A field without seed money is not yet a farm" argues that redress instruments:
options: Need their PARTNERS — a title deed, learnership or tender falls short unless finance, jobs and support arrive together

economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.subject: economics
economics.grade10.public-sector-and-cont.question: The five people in the queue at the gate represent:
options: Five reasons to leave the labour force
The five TYPES of unemployment — frictional, structural, cyclical, seasonal and technological — each needing its own fix

economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.subject: economics
economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.question: Scarcity differs from a shortage because:
options: Scarcity is the PERMANENT condition of insufficient resources; a shortage is a temporary market situation fixable by prices or supply
Shortages are permanent; scarcity is temporary
They are two words for the same thing

economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.subject: economics
economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.question: A millionaire still faces scarcity because:
options: Wants expand with means — and even unlimited money cannot buy unlimited time

economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.subject: economics
economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.question: Scarcity's real force is that it:
options: FORCES RANKING — which want is satisfied first, which waits, which never

economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.subject: economics
economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.question: Bread sold out before noon at the spaza is:
options: A SHORTAGE — temporary, fixed by the delivery van and price adjustment

economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.subject: economics
economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.question: Opportunity cost is defined as:
options: The value of the NEXT BEST alternative sacrificed — not all alternatives forgone
Every alternative given up, added together

economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.subject: economics
economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.question: The R120 calculator whose runner-up was a data bundle has an opportunity cost of:
options: One data bundle — expressed in real terms, not rands
Nothing, since the money was spent anyway

economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.subject: economics
economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.question: The true cost of Thabo's R6 000 machine is:
options: The forgone profit the stock (the next best use) would have earned

economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.subject: economics
economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.question: Every budget debate in a democracy is, properly understood:
options: A fight about tax rates only
An argument about OPPORTUNITY COST — each billion spent is a billion taken from its next-best use

economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.subject: economics
economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.question: The three questions are:
options: WHAT to produce, HOW to produce, FOR WHOM to produce
When, where and why to produce

economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.subject: economics
economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.question: The HOW question carries deep consequences in South Africa because:
options: Labour-intensive methods employ many hands while capital-intensive methods use few — weighty where unemployment is high

economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.subject: economics
economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.question: In a market economy, the three questions are answered by:
options: PRICES — profitable goods get produced, cheapest methods win, output goes to those willing and able to pay

economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.subject: economics
economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.question: South Africa is classified as:
options: A MIXED economy — private markets beside public schools, clinics, grants and state enterprises

economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.subject: economics
economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.question: Economic activity PROMOTES rights when:
options: Employment funds food, shelter, education and dignity — and taxation funds public provision

economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.subject: economics
economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.question: An EXTERNALITY is:
options: A cost paid at the till
A cost landing on third parties that no market price collected — the community breathing the smoke

economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.subject: economics
economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.question: Sustainability means:
options: Producing as much as possible now
Meeting today's needs without robbing tomorrow's

economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.subject: economics
economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.question: The factory-and-river scenario must be answered by:
options: Choosing the side with more marks
Ignoring the pollution if jobs are created
Arguing BOTH sides — employment promoted, health violated — then naming remedies: regulation, taxing the externality, labour-law enforcement

economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.subject: economics
economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.question: The test that sorts shortage from scarcity:
options: Can it be fixed by delivery, price or waiting? Shortage. Is it the permanent wanting-more-than-there-is? Scarcity
Does it happen at a spaza?

economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.subject: economics
economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.question: "Get the phone — now you want the earbuds" illustrates:
options: Wants refilling — why the forever-gap never closes

economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.subject: economics
economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.question: The household with R3 000 after rent asks:
options: "What do we want?" — and buys it all
"What comes FIRST?" — scarcity makes life a defended queue of wants

economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.subject: economics
economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.question: The "hidden price tag" on every choice reads:
options: What ELSE the money or time would have been — the next-best thing now lived without

economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.subject: economics
economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.question: The Saturday shift earning R150 in exam season carries the hidden tag:
options: "One day of matric revision" — which can cost more than the money earned

economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.subject: economics
economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.question: Even FREE things carry the tag because:
options: The afternoon spent had a next-best use — time is a scarce resource

economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.subject: economics
economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.question: "Money measures the front of the tag; life is lived on the back of it" means:
options: Cash purchases are better than credit
Tags should list alternatives by law
The rand price shows what you PAY; the opportunity cost shows what you GIVE UP — and the second is the true price

economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.subject: economics
economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.question: "Rights stop being words on paper" when:
options: The economy works — wages fund school fees, clinic visits and dignity; taxes fund the school's roof

economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.subject: economics
economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.question: "The factory's prices don't include the coughing children" describes:
options: An externality — a cost landing on people who were never part of the deal

economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.subject: economics
economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.question: "Don't feed the family today by burning the table" is the street version of:
options: SUSTAINABILITY — today's needs met without robbing tomorrow's

economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.subject: economics
economics.grade10.scarcity-choice-and-op.question: The two-column habit for the factory scenario means:
options: Choosing jobs over health every time
Choosing health over jobs every time
Counting both columns honestly — jobs, incomes, taxes against health, water, tomorrow's resources — then naming the fixes

economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.subject: economics
economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.question: The state intervenes in markets because:
options: Price rationing can be intolerable for essentials, externalities go uncharged, harmful goods are overconsumed and incomes are unequal

economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.subject: economics
economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.question: Indirect taxes are:
options: Taxes levied on goods and services — VAT, excise duties, the fuel levy — raising revenue AND changing behaviour

economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.subject: economics
economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.question: A subsidy is:
options: The tax in reverse — the state pays part of the cost, making the good cheaper than the market alone would

economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.subject: economics
economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.question: Welfare instruments — grants, public healthcare, no-fee schools — work by:
options: BYPASSING prices — direct provision and transfers placing buying power or services where income failed

economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.subject: economics
economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.question: An indirect tax shifts:
options: The SUPPLY curve LEFTWARD — sellers need a higher price per unit to offer what they offered before
Nothing — only the price label changes

economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.subject: economics
economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.question: After the tax, the burden typically:
options: SPLITS — price rises by less than the full tax, so buyers pay part and sellers absorb part

economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.subject: economics
economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.question: A subsidy's diagram consequences are:
options: Supply left, price up, quantity down
Supply RIGHT — equilibrium price LOWER, quantity HIGHER (cheaper bus rides, more riders)

economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.subject: economics
economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.question: One honest cost of each instrument:
options: Taxes and subsidies have no costs
A tax set too high breeds smuggling; a subsidy must be funded from taxation elsewhere and can be captured by producers

economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.subject: economics
economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.question: A maximum price is only effective (binding) when set:
options: BELOW the equilibrium price — to make an essential affordable

economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.subject: economics
economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.question: The ceiling's permanent consequence is:
options: A surplus the state must buy
A SHORTAGE — quantity demanded exceeds supplied, and the price is legally forbidden from rising to clear it

economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.subject: economics
economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.question: With price rationing broken, the good is rationed instead by:
options: Queues, first-come-first-served, sellers' favourites and per-customer limits

economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.subject: economics
economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.question: The black market arises because:
options: The shortage's pressure leaks into illegal sales above the ceiling — the desperate paying more than the free market price would ever have been

economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.subject: economics
economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.question: A minimum price is set:
options: ABOVE equilibrium, to protect sellers' incomes — historically common for farm produce

economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.subject: economics
economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.question: The floor's consequence is:
options: A SURPLUS — supplied exceeds demanded, and the state typically must buy, store or export the unsold stock
A black market below cost only

economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.subject: economics
economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.question: The minimum wage's mechanical diagram prediction is:
options: More jobs at higher pay for everyone
More labour offered, less demanded — a surplus of labour: unemployment pressure

economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.subject: economics
economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.question: The mature verdict on the minimum wage is:
options: The dignity argument settles it for
A trade-off between protecting the employed and risking the excluded — its actual size an empirical question, measured country by country

economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.subject: economics
economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.question: The referee's four whistles are:
options: Make it dearer (tax), make it cheaper (subsidy), fix the score (price controls), skip the game (welfare)

economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.subject: economics
economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.question: The cigarette tax does "two jobs with one whistle":
options: COLLECTS revenue AND DISCOURAGES smoking through the higher price
Raises and lowers prices at once

economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.subject: economics
economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.question: The referee steps in because the game's natural rule — whoever can pay, plays — is:
options: Sometimes a rule society won't accept for bread, medicine or a working wage

economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.subject: economics
economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.question: Under the bread ceiling, the shelves empty because:
options: At the capped price baking barely pays — many wanting, few baking
The state buys all the bread

economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.subject: economics
economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.question: The cheap bread goes to:
options: Whoever queued from 5 a.m., knows the baker — or pays double in the alley

economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.subject: economics
economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.question: Under the maize floor, the silos overflow because:
options: Buyers buy more at the dear price
Farmers plant everything at the rewarding price while buyers take less — and the price may not fall to clear it

economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.subject: economics
economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.question: The memory trick is:
options: Ceilings make piles; floors make queues
QUEUES under ceilings (pushed low, below equilibrium); PILES on floors (raised high, above equilibrium)

economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.subject: economics
economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.question: Truth one of the wage floor:
options: For everyone employed at the floor — rent paid, children fed, dignity restored, wages spent back into the neighbourhood's circle

economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.subject: economics
economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.question: Truth two of the wage floor:
options: Some firms hire fewer hands — and the squeezed-out-first are the youngest and least skilled; some work slips off the books

economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.subject: economics
economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.question: "Possibly BOTH, about different people" answers:
options: The aunt-versus-cousin argument — the wage can save one family while pricing out another; the balance is measured, not shouted

economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.subject: economics
economics.grade10.taxes-subsidies-and-pr.question: The three-question habit for any intervention:
options: Who proposed it, who opposed it, who won?
How much, how long, how often?
Is it left, right or centre?
What was it FOR, what does the diagram predict, and what ELSE follows?

economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.subject: economics
economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.question: The PPC model's assumptions are:
options: Two goods only; fixed resources; fixed technology; full and efficient employment

economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.subject: economics
economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.question: Every point ON the curve represents:
options: A MAXIMUM — the most of one good obtainable given the chosen amount of the other, with everything employed

economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.subject: economics
economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.question: Moving along the curve from B to C means:
options: MORE maize and FEWER vegetables — the gain on one axis is paid for on the other

economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.subject: economics
economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.question: "The diagram refuses free lunches by construction" means:
options: Points inside the curve are illegal
No movement along the curve exists without giving something up — scarcity and choice are built into the boundary

economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.subject: economics
economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.question: A point INSIDE the curve is:
options: Attainable but INEFFICIENT — resources idle or misused; where recessions and unemployment live on this diagram

economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.subject: economics
economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.question: A point BEYOND the curve is:
options: UNATTAINABLE for now — out of reach until the curve itself moves

economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.subject: economics
economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.question: From A→B the first 10 maize cost 5 vegetables; from E→F the last 10 cost 15. This shows:
options: INCREASING opportunity cost — each extra tonne of maize costs more vegetables than the last

economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.subject: economics
economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.question: The curve bows outward because:
options: Resources are NOT equally suited to all uses — pushing further converts resources that served the other good brilliantly

economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.subject: economics
economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.question: Internal factors that shift the PPC outward include:
options: More/better resources, capital accumulation, education and training, technology, efficiency reforms

economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.subject: economics
economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.question: External factors include:
options: Weather and climate, world markets and prices, imported technology, and shocks like wars and disasters
The choice of point on the curve

economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.subject: economics
economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.question: The outward shift of the PPC IS:
options: ECONOMIC GROWTH drawn — the boundary of capacity itself advancing

economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.subject: economics
economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.question: Unemployment falling moves the economy:
options: From INSIDE toward the curve — recovery, not growth; three improvements, three different pictures

economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.subject: economics
economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.question: The distance from an inside point to the curve measures:
options: Output that could exist and does not — houses unbuilt, food ungrown, services undelivered

economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.subject: economics
economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.question: The chained consequences of the gap run:
options: Lost output → lost incomes → lost spending → lost tax revenue — the circular flow turning smaller
Lost output → lower prices → more demand

economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.subject: economics
economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.question: Persistent idleness "pulls tomorrow's curve inward" because:
options: Skills decay in long unemployment, machines rust, the discouraged stop seeking — capacity itself erodes

economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.subject: economics
economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.question: The two policy tasks, in order:
options: Move the curve, then reach it
Choose a point, then defend it
GET TO the curve (employ what exists — the cheapest growth), THEN MOVE the curve (investment, education, technology)

economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.subject: economics
economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.question: The bakery menu's "iron rule" is:
options: Every extra brown loaf is PAID FOR in whites — the fixed day makes every combination a trade

economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.subject: economics
economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.question: Drawing the menu as dots and joining them produces:
options: The curved boundary of the possible day — the production possibility curve

economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.subject: economics
economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.question: A country's PPC is the bakery's menu with:
options: Bigger ovens — fixed resources, two products for simplicity, a boundary that says choose your mix

economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.subject: economics
economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.question: The FULL day lands:
options: ON the line — the most the bakery can do in its chosen mix, with no point on the line being 'the right one'

economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.subject: economics
economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.question: The LAZY day — baker off sick, oven idle, flour forgotten — lands:
options: INSIDE the line — waste's address; for a country, where unemployment lives

economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.subject: economics
economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.question: 50 whites AND 40 browns in one day is:
options: The DREAM day — beyond the line, tomorrow's target waiting for the bakery itself to change

economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.subject: economics
economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.question: The browns "get more expensive as you bake more" because:
options: The best-suited bakers and pans are used first — pushing further converts white-bread specialists to work they do slowly

economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.subject: economics
economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.question: Buying a second oven shifts the line:
options: OUTWARD — yesterday's impossible combinations join the menu: growth

economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.subject: economics
economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.question: The three improvements kept apart are:
options: Different MIX (along the line), fixing a lazy day (inside back TO the line — recovery), and the line ADVANCING (growth alone)

economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.subject: economics
economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.question: The lazy day's full cost includes:
options: Unearned wages unspent at the spaza, unpaid tax toward the clinic, and idle bakers losing their speed — tomorrow's full day shrinking

economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.subject: economics
economics.grade10.the-production-possibi.question: South Africa's "first, cheapest growth" is:
options: Walking back to the boundary — employing the hands already inside the line — THEN growing the oven

economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.subject: economics
economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.question: The strictly unemployed are working-age people who are:
options: Without work, AVAILABLE for work, and ACTIVELY SEEKING it

economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.subject: economics
economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.question: Saying South African unemployment is STRUCTURAL rather than merely cyclical means:
options: It persists through upswings — so the business cycle alone cannot explain it

economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.subject: economics
economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.question: Long-term unemployment makes re-entry harder because:
options: Employers are legally barred from hiring the long-term unemployed
It erodes skills, networks and confidence the longer it lasts

economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.subject: economics
economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.question: Why will growth alone not clear South Africa's unemployment?
options: Growth that is capital-intensive or skill-concentrated can raise output while bypassing the unskilled

economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.subject: economics
economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.question: FRICTIONAL unemployment describes:
options: People BETWEEN jobs — short-term search time that exists in every healthy economy; remedied by better information and matching

economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.subject: economics
economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.question: STRUCTURAL unemployment is:
options: A MISMATCH between the skills or locations workers have and those employers need — South Africa's dominant type

economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.subject: economics
economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.question: Cyclical unemployment is remedied by:
options: DEMAND — state spending, lower interest rates, export growth restoring the derived demand for labour

economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.subject: economics
economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.question: The mineworker whose shaft closed and whose skills fit no growing sector is:
options: STRUCTURALLY unemployed — needing retraining and spatial remedies, not merely better adverts

economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.subject: economics
economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.question: Structural and historical causes of SA unemployment include:
options: Capital-intensive mining and manufacturing, a skills pipeline misaligned with employer needs, and apartheid's spatial legacy

economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.subject: economics
economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.question: For the ECONOMY, unemployment means:
options: Output forgone (producing inside the PPC), weaker aggregate demand, lost tax revenue as social spending needs rise, and decaying skills

economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.subject: economics
economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.question: The self-reinforcing loop runs:
options: Unemployment raises spending, which raises production
Unemployment has no effect on production
Unemployment lowers spending → lower spending lowers production → lower production lowers hiring
Hiring falls only when wages rise

economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.subject: economics
economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.question: For the INDIVIDUAL, unemployment is:
options: Only a temporary loss of wages
A statistical category with no personal effect
Lost income and poverty, grant and family dependence, eroded skills and confidence, with documented effects on health, dignity and family stability

economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.subject: economics
economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.question: Growth of production creates jobs through:
options: DERIVED demand — more production requires more labour, especially where growth favours labour-intensive sectors

economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.subject: economics
economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.question: Public works programmes are best judged as:
options: A permanent replacement for private employment
A BRIDGE, not a destination — immediate income, experience and assets, but temporary, budget-funded jobs that must lead onward
A cure for frictional unemployment only

economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.subject: economics
economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.question: The UIF's crucial limitation is that it:
options: Only helps those who WERE formally employed — never the never-employed young person, South Africa's largest unemployed group

economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.subject: economics
economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.question: The mature conclusion the examination wants:
options: DIAGNOSE before prescribing — cyclical needs demand, frictional needs information, structural needs education, training and spatial remedies, with works bridging and insurance cushioning

economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.subject: economics
economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.question: "Experience is required to get the experience" describes:
options: The cruel loop facing first-time work-seekers, who are the front of every SA unemployment number
The frictional gap between school and work only

economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.subject: economics
economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.question: The engineering firm with a three-person queue phoning agencies shows:
options: The SPLIT BY SKILL — same town, opposite problem: scarce skills short-queued, unskilled labour flooded

economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.subject: economics
economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.question: The people who "stopped coming" to the queue:
options: Are counted in the strict rate
Left because they stopped believing the gate opens — invisible to the strict count, visible in the expanded one, and the deepest part of the problem

economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.subject: economics
economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.question: The graduate who finished in November and starts in February is:
options: In the GAP — frictional unemployment, fixed by faster matching and information

economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.subject: economics
economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.question: The matriculant in a town whose only vacancies demand "artisan, three years' experience" illustrates:
options: A MISMATCH — structural unemployment, needing training, trades and closing the distance between people and jobs

economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.subject: economics
economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.question: The retrenchment letter arriving when orders dried up nationwide is:
options: CYCLICAL — it lifts when the economy lifts; the fix is demand

economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.subject: economics
economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.question: "Anyone who offers one cure for all five stories is selling something" means:
options: DIAGNOSE BEFORE YOU PRESCRIBE — five causes need five different responses

economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.subject: economics
economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.question: "Growing in what — and does it need people?" matters because:
options: A machine-heavy expansion can add billions in output and few jobs, while tourism, farming, construction and small business add far more hands per rand

economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.subject: economics
economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.question: The honest limit of the public works BRIDGE is:
options: If the programme doesn't lead to a skill, certificate or next job, the bridge ends in the same river

economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.subject: economics
economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.question: The NET (UIF) protects the economy as well as the worker because:
options: Benefits keep spending in the shops during downswings — stabilising the circular flow

economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.subject: economics
economics.grade10.unemployment-causes-co.question: "A net with a hole where the young stand" means:
options: You can only claim from a job you HAD — the never-employed young person has paid nothing in and receives nothing out

economics.grade10.value-utility-and-mark.subject: economics
economics.grade10.value-utility-and-mark.question: Utility is SUBJECTIVE, meaning:
options: It lives in the user, not the object — the same umbrella is priceless in a storm and useless on a clear day

economics.grade10.value-utility-and-mark.subject: economics
economics.grade10.value-utility-and-mark.question: Value in use and value in exchange differ in that:
options: Use-value is how useful a thing is to its owner; exchange-value is what it can fetch when traded
Exchange value applies only to exports
Use value is measured in money

economics.grade10.value-utility-and-mark.subject: economics
economics.grade10.value-utility-and-mark.question: The water-diamond paradox resolves because exchange value is governed by:
options: SCARCITY relative to wants, and the utility of the NEXT unit — plenty cheapens, scarcity dearens

economics.grade10.value-utility-and-mark.subject: economics
economics.grade10.value-utility-and-mark.question: Price is best defined as:
options: Value in EXCHANGE expressed in money — one language for all worths

economics.grade10.value-utility-and-mark.subject: economics
economics.grade10.value-utility-and-mark.question: The perfect market's conditions include:
options: Many buyers and sellers, homogeneous product, perfect knowledge, free entry and exit
One seller, unique product, secret prices

economics.grade10.value-utility-and-mark.subject: economics
economics.grade10.value-utility-and-mark.question: Under perfect conditions, every participant is a:
options: PRICE TAKER — the market's crossing point sets the price; each simply accepts it

economics.grade10.value-utility-and-mark.subject: economics
economics.grade10.value-utility-and-mark.question: Banks, cellphone networks and fuel companies exemplify:
