economics.grade11.environmental-deterior.subject: economics
economics.grade11.environmental-deterior.question: Because the smoke's cost reaches no invoice, the market:
options: Orders more bricks — and more smoke — than the full cost would justify

economics.grade11.environmental-deterior.subject: economics
economics.grade11.environmental-deterior.question: Each fisherman taking 'one more fish' empties the river because each is:
options: Individually sensible — full benefit to himself, shared cost to everyone

economics.grade11.environmental-deterior.subject: economics
economics.grade11.environmental-deterior.question: Who is missing from the market's calculations in both stories?
options: Future generations, who place no orders today

economics.grade11.environmental-deterior.subject: economics
economics.grade11.environmental-deterior.question: The plastic bag levy works by:
options: Making the bag cost something, so it stops being free and becomes a choice

economics.grade11.environmental-deterior.subject: economics
economics.grade11.environmental-deterior.question: 'The market's own greed is harnessed' means that once smoke has a price:
options: Cutting pollution becomes profitable saving rather than charity

economics.grade11.environmental-deterior.subject: economics
economics.grade11.environmental-deterior.question: Giving a village a permanent fishing quota flips behaviour because:
options: Next year's fish already belong to the owners, so gentle harvesting pays them
Quotas increase the fish population directly

economics.grade11.environmental-deterior.subject: economics
economics.grade11.environmental-deterior.question: Countries sign climate agreements together mainly to:
options: Stop free-riding — one country cutting alone helps little and costs much

economics.grade11.environmental-deterior.subject: economics
economics.grade11.environmental-deterior.question: 'Eat the harvest, never the seed' translates into economics as:
options: Use natural stocks slower than they renew

economics.grade11.environmental-deterior.subject: economics
economics.grade11.environmental-deterior.question: 'Digging up the family gold to buy groceries' warns that non-renewable wealth should be:
options: Turned into lasting assets — skills, infrastructure, working towns
Divided equally among citizens in cash

economics.grade11.environmental-deterior.subject: economics
economics.grade11.environmental-deterior.question: 'Save the park but starve the village beside it, and the village will not save the park' tests which leg of sustainability?
options: Social — costs and benefits must be shared fairly

economics.grade11.environmental-deterior.subject: economics
economics.grade11.environmental-deterior.question: South Africa's just transition attempts to:
options: Close coal towns immediately with no support
Build clean energy fast while retraining workers and rebuilding coal regions, with wealthy nations helping to pay

economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.question: Which pairing of factor and remuneration is completely correct?
options: Natural resources — rent; labour — wages and salaries; capital — interest; entrepreneurship — profit
Natural resources — profit; labour — rent; capital — wages; entrepreneurship — interest
Natural resources — interest; labour — profit; capital — rent; entrepreneurship — wages
All four factors are rewarded with dividends

economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.question: In economics, capital means:
options: The money in a business bank account
REAL capital — the man-made means of production such as machinery, buildings and vehicles, which were produced in order to produce further goods
Shares listed on the stock exchange

economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.question: Households and firms meet in the FACTOR market when:
options: Firms sell finished goods to households
Households supply land, labour, capital and enterprise, and firms pay rent, wages, interest and profit for them

economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.question: Why are dividends NOT a factor remuneration?
options: Because they are illegal in South Africa
Because only government may pay them
Because they are the same thing as interest
Because they are profit being distributed to shareholders after that profit has already been earned as the reward to entrepreneurship

economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.question: Rent on a well-placed Durban shop site is high mainly because:
options: The total supply of that site is FIXED, so its price is determined almost entirely by demand
It cost a great deal to manufacture the site
The municipality sets the rent by law

economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.question: Labour is described as PERISHABLE because:
options: A day of labour not worked is lost permanently — it cannot be stored, which is why unemployment is a pure loss rather than a postponement

economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.question: Under the Mineral and Petroleum Resources Development Act, mineral rights in South Africa:
options: Belong to the mining company that finds them
Vest in the STATE, with companies holding rights by licence

economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.question: High unemployment existing alongside a shortage of high-level skills is best described as:
options: A fall in the labour force
A skills MISMATCH — the skills supplied are not the skills demanded

economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.question: The Gqeberha firm has sales of R4 000 000 and buys in R1 500 000 of steel, electricity and services. Its VALUE ADDED is:

economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.question: Wages R1 600 000, rent R240 000, interest R160 000 and depreciation R200 000 come out of value added of R2 500 000. Profit is therefore:

economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.question: Profit is called a RESIDUAL because:
options: It is whatever remains after the contractual payments to the other factors, and it can be negative
It is fixed by contract at the start of the year

economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.question: The R1 500 000 of bought-in steel and electricity is excluded from the factor share-out because:
options: It is not a real cost
It is INTERMEDIATE consumption — it already paid wages and profits inside the supplying firms, so counting it again would be double counting

economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.question: The Integrated Development Plan (IDP) is:
options: The plan every municipality must adopt and review annually, inside which local economic development sits
The Reserve Bank's monetary policy statement
A company's business plan submitted to SARS

economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.question: Why does a lack of secure land tenure block access to the factors of production?
options: Because farming is banned without title
Because without registered title there is no COLLATERAL, so banks will not lend and the venture never starts
Because land without title has no productive use

economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.question: Which list gives elements of the B-BBEE scorecard?
options: Inflation, unemployment, growth and the exchange rate
Ownership, management control, skills development, enterprise and supplier development, and socio-economic development

economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.question: Under the Preferential Procurement Policy Framework Act, the 80/20 and 90/10 systems mean that:
options: Only 20 per cent of tenders may be awarded
Government pays 90 per cent of the price
Most points are awarded for price and a fixed remainder for specific goals such as transformation, with 90/10 applied to larger contracts

economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.question: In the taxi business, the kombi, tyres and card machine are:
options: CAPITAL — things people built in order to earn with, whose funding costs interest

economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.question: The person who spotted the route, borrowed for the kombi, hires the driver and carries the loss when the gearbox goes is supplying:

economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.question: "Money is not capital" means:
options: The R400 000 in the account is not the factor of production — the kombi it buys is
Only cash counts as a factor

economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.question: The kombi takes R60 000 in fares and spends R22 500 on diesel, tyres and repairs bought from other businesses. The value it ADDED is:

economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.question: Wages R18 000, rank fees R2 500, interest R4 000 and R6 000 set aside for wear come out of R37 500. The owner is left with:

economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.question: The order of payment in the taxi business shows that:
options: The owner is paid first, at a guaranteed amount
Everyone else is paid FIRST at agreed amounts and the owner LAST at an amount nobody promised — which is why the owner decides
Interest is paid only if there is profit

economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.question: Why is the R22 500 of diesel and tyres left out of the taxi's value added?
options: It is not a real expense
It already paid a wage at the garage and a profit at the tyre factory, so counting it again would count the same money twice

economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.question: "A district with good soil and no packhouse sends its tomatoes away raw and buys the sauce back" illustrates:
options: The purpose of local economic planning — combining a district's factors locally so the value added stays at home
The circular flow of money only

economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.question: The three bakers with the same idea show that access depends on:
options: The quality of the business idea alone
Collateral, information and transport — not the quality of the idea

economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.question: Attending the ward meeting matters economically because:
options: It is compulsory by law for every resident
The plan is written whether you are there or not, and the road, clinic and trading stalls go where the plan says
It replaces the need for tenders

economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.factors-of-production-.question: The economic point of empowerment procurement is that:
options: It is a form of charity to small firms
It lowers the price government pays
Demand creates factor incomes — so pointing a share of the state's enormous purchasing at excluded suppliers redirects income toward them

economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.subject: economics
economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.question: The three economic questions every system must answer are:
options: WHAT to produce, HOW to produce it, and FOR WHOM to produce
Who governs, who votes and who taxes

economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.subject: economics
economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.question: The underlying variable that separates one economic system from another is:
options: Who owns and controls the MEANS OF PRODUCTION, because ownership determines who has the right to decide

economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.subject: economics
economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.question: In a country with very high unemployment, the HOW question is particularly sharp because:
options: There is nothing left to produce
The choice between labour-intensive and capital-intensive methods decides how many people work

economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.subject: economics
economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.question: Why must an economic system not be confused with a political system?
options: Because economic systems are chosen by voters
Because political systems have no effect on the economy
Because economic systems are classified by ownership and co-ordination, political systems by how power is held and transferred — two separate axes

economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.subject: economics
economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.question: The price mechanism co-ordinates a free market because:
options: A rise in demand raises price, which raises profit, which attracts producers and resources, which expands supply — prices carrying both information and incentive
Producers agree on prices in advance
Consumers vote for prices each year

economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.subject: economics
economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.question: In a free market, the FOR WHOM question is answered by:
options: INCOME — those with the most purchasing power obtain the most output
Length of service to the state

economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.subject: economics
economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.question: Street lighting is under-supplied by a pure market because:
options: It is too expensive to produce
It is a PUBLIC GOOD — non-excludable, so nobody will pay for it voluntarily
It creates a positive externality for producers

economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.subject: economics
economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.question: A factory polluting a river is a market failure because:
options: The factory earns too much profit
The factory does not pay for the damage it causes, so its price is wrong and too much is produced

economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.subject: economics
economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.question: In a centrally planned economy, the WHAT question is answered by:
options: The central planning authority, according to its assessment of social need

economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.subject: economics
economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.question: Which is a genuine strength of central planning, fairly stated?
options: National resources can be mobilised very rapidly toward a chosen objective, and basic needs can be guaranteed regardless of income
It responds instantly to changing tastes

economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.subject: economics
economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.question: The INFORMATION problem in a planned economy means that:
options: No central office can know the millions of local facts about wants and costs that prices summarise automatically, so plans are always partly wrong

economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.subject: economics
economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.question: Queues for some goods alongside warehouses of others occur under central planning because:
options: Administered prices cannot adjust, so shortages and surpluses are not corrected the way a market price would correct them

economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.subject: economics
economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.question: In a mixed economy, the FOR WHOM question is answered by:
options: Income earned in the market, then MODIFIED by redistribution through progressive tax, grants, free basic services and no-fee schools
Ability to pay alone, with no adjustment

economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.subject: economics
economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.question: Which set of features shows South Africa to be a MIXED economy?
options: Only state ownership of all mines and factories

Constitutional protection of property alongside socio-economic rights, mostly private production alongside state-owned enterprises in electricity, rail and ports, market regulators, and large-scale redistribution
No government participation in the economy at all
Prices fixed by a central planning office

economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.subject: economics
economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.question: A DUALISTIC economy is one in which:
options: A modern, formal, capital-intensive economy coexists with an informal, survivalist, low-productivity one inside the same country

economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.subject: economics
economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.question: The structural causes of South Africa's dualism are best given as:
options: Differences in individual effort and ambition
The weather and the mineral endowment

Land dispossession and migrant labour, apartheid spatial planning that placed people far from economic centres, and an unequal education system that withheld the qualifications the formal economy demands

economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.subject: economics
economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.question: The tuckshop, where vetkoek sell out and tomorrow more vetkoek appear, represents:
options: The free market — the till does the talking and your wallet decides your plate

economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.subject: economics
economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.question: The feeding scheme, with one official setting the term's menu, represents:
options: The centrally planned economy — fairer plates, worse information

economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.subject: economics
economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.question: A school running both a feeding scheme and a tuckshop is a model of:
options: The MIXED economy — which is what South Africa is

economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.subject: economics
economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.question: "A price is a message" means that:
options: Prices carry information about what people want and what is scarce, gathered automatically and for free from millions of transactions
Prices are set by government notice

economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.subject: economics
economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.question: When a planner's guess is wrong, the mistake persists because:
options: The price cannot correct it — the price was fixed by the office rather than discovered in a market
There is no money in circulation

economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.subject: economics
economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.question: The market's "one cruel habit" is that:
options: It only hears money — a hungry learner with no coins sends no message at all, which is why every country keeps a feeding scheme beside its tuckshop

economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.subject: economics
economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.question: The office tower and the airtime table an hour away illustrate:
options: Dualism — a formal, capital-rich economy and a survivalist, informal one inside one country

economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.subject: economics
economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.question: Why can the airtime seller not simply borrow and grow?
options: Because banks lend against collateral, and someone with nothing to pledge cannot borrow the very thing that would let her grow
Because she does not want to
Because interest rates are fixed by the state

economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.subject: economics
economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.question: "Effort" is a poor explanation of dualism because:
options: The real separators are structural — concentrated ownership, distance from work, unequal schooling and the collateral barrier — none of which is about how hard anyone tries

economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.subject: economics
economics.grade11.free-market-planned-an.question: Grants, no-fee schools, free basic services, land reform, small-business finance and public transport are best described as:
options: Features of a purely planned economy
The deliberate mixed-economy attempts to build doors between the first and second economies

economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.question: The lesson's working test for globalisation is that:
options: Decisions on one continent change prices, jobs and incomes on another, faster than a generation ago
Every country produces everything it needs

economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.question: The shipping container drove globalisation by:
options: Collapsing the cost of moving goods — one standard box from ship to truck to train without unpacking

economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.question: A firm slicing production into stages placed wherever each is cheapest creates a:

economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.question: Which cause belongs to the POLICY family rather than the technology family?
options: Tariff reductions leading to the WTO in 1995

economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.question: South Africa's motor industry is cited as a gain from globalisation because:
options: It only sells inside South Africa
Global carmakers built world-scale plants here, supporting over 100 000 jobs
It is protected from all trade

economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.question: The clothing towns of Newcastle and parts of the Western Cape illustrate:
options: The losses column — jobs destroyed when cheap imports arrived after tariffs fell

economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.question: The 2008 crisis reached South African workers because:
options: The rand was fixed to the dollar
Our customers' economies stopped buying — financial contagion through an interconnected system

economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.question: The 'race to the bottom' refers to:
options: Mobile multinationals playing governments against each other on taxes and standards, while less mobile workers lose bargaining power
Countries competing to cut prices of exports

economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.question: The North/South divide labels are described as:
options: Strict geography — everything below the equator is South
Economic shorthand — Australia is southern on the map but Northern in the economy

economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.question: The terms-of-trade treadmill means many Southern economies:
options: Set world prices for their exports
Find their raw exports buying fewer and fewer manufactured imports over time

economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.question: The debt mechanism squeezes Southern budgets when:
options: World interest rates rise or their currencies fall, ballooning foreign-currency repayments
The IMF cancels all debts yearly

economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.question: Higher tariffs on processed goods than on raw materials historically discouraged the South from:

economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.question: South Africa's openness is evidenced by:
options: Exports plus imports amounting to well over half of GDP

economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.question: The AfCFTA is described as the great opportunity because:
options: It removes all taxes in South Africa
Africa buys South Africa's manufactured goods, not just its ores

economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.question: 'South Africa is the North/South divide in one country' because:
options: Our provinces trade with different continents
The north of the country is richer than the south
Northern-style finance thrives in Sandton while exports stay raw-commodity dependent
We belong to no trade blocs

economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.question: The two-handed policy debate weighs deeper integration against:
options: Strategic protection — tariffs and local-content rules while industries rebuild

economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.question: The phone-as-map exercise shows a single phone touching at least:
options: Six countries across design, materials, assembly and connectivity

economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.question: Door one — 'it had to become possible' — was opened by:
options: Containers making goods cheap to move and cables making information instant

economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.question: South Africa walked back through door two — 'allowed to move' — when it:
options: Rejoined world markets and investors after 1994

economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.question: Cheap imports are called 'a raise nobody announces' because:
options: Employers must raise wages by law
The same wage buys more when world-shop prices are lower

economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.question: The Newcastle story shows that trade's losses land on:
options: Whoever competes head-on with the world's cheapest producers

economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.question: 'Connected means exposed' summarises:
options: How a foreign crisis like 2008 travels to South African jobs within a year

economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.question: The economist's answer to 'is globalisation good or bad?' is that it:
options: Grows the total while moving the shares — so policy must spread gains and cushion losses

economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.question: In the coffee-cup story, the South earns cents while the North earns rands because:
options: Coffee cannot grow in the North
The finishing — roasting, branding, retail — is where the money lives, and it happens up north

economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.question: The three weights on the South named in this section are:
options: Raw-for-made trade, foreign-currency debt, and weak voice in rule-writing institutions

economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.question: The African free trade agreement is 'the South's most direct answer' because it aims to:
options: Raise tariffs against all imports permanently
Move African economies to the North
Keep the finishing — and the rands — inside Africa by letting Africa sell made goods to Africa

economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.subject: economics
economics.grade11.globalisation-and-the-.question: Which development is MOVING the North/South map?
options: China and India pulling the world's economic centre southward, and BRICS pressing for Southern voice
The North giving up manufacturing entirely

economics.grade11.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade11.growth-development-and.question: Economic growth is properly measured as:
options: The increase in REAL GDP — inflation stripped out — and per capita, since a faster-growing population means shrinking shares
The number of new companies registered

economics.grade11.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade11.growth-development-and.question: On the Lorenz curve, deeper sag below the diagonal means:
options: WORSE inequality — the poorest have collected a smaller share of total income at each point in the line-up

economics.grade11.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade11.growth-development-and.question: South Africa's Gini coefficient of around 0,65 signifies:
options: Inequality among the HIGHEST ever recorded — the anchor fact of every redistribution essay

economics.grade11.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade11.growth-development-and.question: "Redistribution needs growth, and growth needs redistribution" means:
options: Growth should wait for equality first
Grants and services need a growing tax base to fund them, while a widening of participation feeds growth — the pot must grow WHILE the shares move

economics.grade11.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade11.growth-development-and.question: The Human Development Index combines:
options: LIFE EXPECTANCY, EDUCATION and INCOME per person — so a healthier, better-schooled country can outrank a richer one

economics.grade11.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade11.growth-development-and.question: "Growth without development" describes:
options: GDP rising while health, education and opportunity STAGNATE — the distinction the topic is built on

economics.grade11.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade11.growth-development-and.question: South Africa's succession of development plans runs:
options: RDP for basic needs, GEAR for stability, AsgiSA for constraints, NDP as the current framework

economics.grade11.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade11.growth-development-and.question: Indigenous knowledge systems matter for development because they:
options: Cut costs, fit local conditions and carry OWNERSHIP that imported blueprints lack — development done WITH people compounds

economics.grade11.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade11.growth-development-and.question: The two families of globalisation's causes are:
options: TECHNOLOGY making it possible — containers, cables, computing — and POLICY making it permitted — tariff cuts, freed finance, reopened economies

economics.grade11.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade11.growth-development-and.question: The 2008 crisis reaching South African factories within a year demonstrates:
options: CONTAGION — in one interconnected system, a foreign financial collapse destroys jobs far from its origin

economics.grade11.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade11.growth-development-and.question: The terms-of-trade treadmill traps Southern economies because:
options: They export too little raw material
Raw export prices SWING and SAG over time against the manufactured goods they import — selling raw and buying made buys less each year
Northern countries buy nothing from the South

economics.grade11.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade11.growth-development-and.question: The balanced verdict on globalisation is that it:
options: GROWS the world's total while MOVING the shares — so policy must capture gains and cushion losses

economics.grade11.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade11.growth-development-and.question: A negative externality makes the market fail because the outside cost is:
options: Priced at ZERO by the market — so the product is too cheap and society gets TOO MUCH of it
