economics.grade12.balance-of-payments-an.question: Even when Anna is better at BOTH baking and farming, she still gains by trading with Sipho because:
options: An hour of baking costs Anna two chickens but costs Sipho almost nothing — her baking hour is expensive to her, so she should pour it into the chicken run

economics.grade12.balance-of-payments-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.balance-of-payments-an.question: "Countries are Sipho and Anna with flags" means:
options: Nations, like the neighbours, gain by doing what costs them least and trading for the rest
Trade requires a formal treaty first

economics.grade12.balance-of-payments-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.balance-of-payments-an.question: The catch at the fence — Anna will not take bread coupons forever — points to:
options: The question of whose money settles the deal — the foreign exchange problem

economics.grade12.balance-of-payments-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.balance-of-payments-an.question: The queue BUYING dollars with rands contains:
options: The fuel importer, the phone importer, the family paying overseas fees and the fund buying American shares
The coal exporter and the wine estate

economics.grade12.balance-of-payments-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.balance-of-payments-an.question: A long queue at the buy-dollars window and a short queue at the sell window means:
options: The dollar gets dearer and the rand weakens — depreciation
The Reserve Bank must print dollars

economics.grade12.balance-of-payments-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.balance-of-payments-an.question: "Foreign funds fall in love with our bonds" moves the rand by:
options: Lengthening the buy-dollar queue and weakening the rand
Having no effect on the market
Bringing dollars to the sell window, so the rand firms — appreciation

economics.grade12.balance-of-payments-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.balance-of-payments-an.question: "Floating is bumpy but honest; fixed is calm until it snaps" summarises:
options: Why South Africa fixes the rand to the dollar
The difference between demand and supply
Floating rates absorb shocks with volatility, while fixed rates give calm certainty until speculators bet the defence must break

economics.grade12.balance-of-payments-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.balance-of-payments-an.question: In the family notebook, the earning and spending columns, the covering column, and the tin on the shelf correspond to:
options: The current account, the financial account, and the official reserves
The budget, the deficit and the Laffer curve

economics.grade12.balance-of-payments-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.balance-of-payments-an.question: The uncle who starts adding conditions to his loans stands for:
options: The IMF — the lender approached when nobody else will cover the gap, whose conditions are as unwelcome nationally as at the kitchen table

economics.grade12.balance-of-payments-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.balance-of-payments-an.question: The depreciating rand is the family's labour getting cheaper to the world, which corrects the gap by:
options: Raising the price of exports abroad
Making our goods a bargain abroad and imports dear at home, so export volumes rise and import volumes shrink

economics.grade12.balance-of-payments-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.balance-of-payments-an.question: Matching the cure to the disease means:
options: Using all four corrections at once in every case
Never using direct controls under any circumstances
A family that overspends needs the belt — demand restraint — while one whose labour is overpriced needs the price cut — depreciation

economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.question: Market failure is best defined as:
options: The market producing quantities different from the socially optimal ones, so a better allocation could raise society's welfare
Any situation where prices are high

economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.question: The market for streetlights never forms at all because:
options: Streetlights are too expensive to build
Non-rivalry and non-excludability mean no firm can charge users — a missing market, failure at its most absolute

economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.question: Miners in a dying coal town who cannot retrain or relocate illustrate which cause of market failure?
options: Immobility of factors of production — the standing South African case being structural unemployment

economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.question: "A market can be perfectly efficient and still leave a nation hungry" refers to:
options: Inequality — markets weight demand by purchasing power, so unmet needs backed by no money attract no resources

economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.question: Social cost equals:
options: The price paid by the consumer

economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.question: On the polluting paper mill diagram, the marginal social cost curve:
options: Lies below the private cost curve
Runs parallel above the marginal private cost curve, the vertical gap being the external cost per ton

economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.question: The market equilibrium for the polluting good compared with society's optimum shows:
options: Smaller output at a higher price
Larger output at a lower price — the market over-produces and under-prices the polluting good

economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.question: Vaccination is under-produced by the market because:
options: Demand for vaccines is perfectly elastic
The market demand curve counts only the private benefit, ignoring the external benefit to everyone the vaccinated person never infects

economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.question: A tax set equal to the external cost per unit corrects a negative externality by:
options: Lifting the private cost curve onto the social cost curve, so the market itself chooses the smaller, socially optimal quantity

economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.question: South Africa's carbon tax, sin taxes and the sugary drinks levy are examples of:
options: Taxes on external costs — making the polluter or consumer pay the social cost

economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.question: A maximum price set below equilibrium for an essential good typically causes:
options: Shortages and queues — the standard side effect of holding price below the market-clearing level

economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.question: The evaluation point that completes any answer on the state's toolkit is:
options: Every instrument has a cost — wrong levels, financing burdens, distortions — and each intervention risks public sector failure, so each needs its own justification

economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.question: Public projects need cost-benefit analysis rather than market profit tests because:
options: Many of their costs and benefits are external, unpriced or decades away — profit measures only the private slice

economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.question: Future benefits are DISCOUNTED in CBA because:
options: Future benefits are always uncertain fabrications
A rand of benefit in twenty years is worth less than a rand today, so distant flows must be shrunk before adding
Discounting doubles the value of a project

economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.question: A high discount rate in a climate-related CBA effectively:
options: Has no effect on the outcome
Silences future generations by shrinking distant benefits toward zero — a moral choice disguised as arithmetic

economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.question: "A project can pass while hurting the poorest" warns that CBA:
options: Sums rands without asking whose they are — distribution must be judged alongside the total

economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.question: The honest cost of the R40 chicken is R45 because:
options: The village pays roughly R5 per chicken in boiled water, clinic visits and lost garden yield — a bill that never reaches the farm or buyer
The farm underpays its workers by R5

economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.question: Because chickens LOOK R5 cheaper than they truly are:
options: Fewer chickens are sold than society wants
People buy more of them than they would at the honest price — the market over-produces the harmful good

economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.question: The evening classes stay half-empty because:
options: Students pay for the whole benefit but capture only part of it — the village's share of the gain is not counted in anyone's decision to enrol
The classes have no external effects

economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.question: The one-sentence pattern of the riverbank is:
options: A missing bill makes too many chickens; a missing thank-you makes too few classes — external costs over-produce, external benefits under-produce

economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.question: The R5 chicken levy is elegant because:
options: Government never orders the farm to do anything — it corrects the price and lets the market choose the smaller quantity itself

economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.question: Subsidising evening classes down to R20 is justified because:
options: Society keeps part of the benefit, so society pays for that part — the missing thank-you delivered

economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.question: "Poison has no correct price" argues that:
options: When harm is grave enough, regulation — an outright rule like no dumping near the river — beats merely taxing the behaviour

economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.question: "Good policy is choosing the smaller failure" means:
options: States always fail worse than markets
Markets always fail worse than states
Both markets and state fixes can fail, so each case must weigh the market's failure against the state's likely failure in correcting it

economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.question: The dam cannot be judged by market prices because:
options: Half of what matters — drowned fields, lost wetlands, prevented floods — carries no market price
Government projects are exempt from prices

economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.question: The wetland is valued in the CBA at:
options: At least what a treatment plant doing the same water-cleaning job would cost
The price of the land if sold

economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.question: When three projects compete for one budget, CBA ranks them by:
options: Benefit per rand — the benefit-cost ratio

economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.causes-consequences-an.question: The two-line caution on CBA is:
options: It is always accurate and always fair
It should never be used for dams
Champions can game the counting, and the page adds rands without asking whose — so watch for optimism bias and ask about compensating the losers

economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.question: The three tiers of government in South Africa, with an example function each, are:
options: National (policy and departments such as police), provincial (schools and hospitals), local (water, refuse and municipal roads)
Parliament, the courts and the Reserve Bank
The IMF, the World Bank and the WTO

economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.question: A PUBLIC good is defined by being:
options: Free of charge and produced by any firm
Non-rivalrous (one person's use leaves no less for another) and non-excludable (non-payers cannot be fenced out)
Any good sold by a state-owned enterprise

economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.question: The FREE-RIDER problem means that:
options: Since non-payers cannot be excluded from a public good, everyone waits for others to pay and no private firm can supply it
Imports enter the country without duties

economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.question: Basic education and vaccination are called MERIT goods because:
options: They are awarded for good performance
Their benefits spill over to society, so the market left alone provides too little of them

economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.question: Accountability is a provisioning problem because:
options: The link between paying and receiving is cut — officials spend money that is not theirs and voters discipline them only every five years
Taxes are too low to fund services
Customers can easily switch to another government

economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.question: Assessing needs is hard for the state because:
options: Unlike a market reading demand off prices, the state must estimate need through surveys, censuses and politics — and the loudest voice is not always the greatest need
Prices always reveal need perfectly to government

economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.question: The parastatal problem, with Eskom as the standing example, is that state-owned enterprises:
options: Must run commercially while also serving social goals, and the tension shows in debt and failing delivery

economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.question: The five macroeconomic objectives of the public sector are:
options: Higher tariffs, lower wages, more exports, less saving, stable gold prices
Free water, free electricity, free transport, free housing, free data
Economic growth, full employment, price stability, exchange-rate stability and economic equity

economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.question: Direct and indirect taxes are, respectively:
options: Taxes on income such as personal and company tax; taxes on spending such as VAT and excise duties
Taxes paid in cash; taxes paid electronically

economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.question: VAT is described as regressive in effect because:
options: The poor spend a larger share of their income, so a flat rate on spending takes a larger share of a poor household's income
It is zero-rated on luxury goods

economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.question: A budget DEFICIT is:
options: Spending exceeding revenue, financed by issuing government bonds that accumulate as public debt
The total of all taxes collected

economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.question: On the Laffer curve, tax revenue is zero at BOTH a zero rate and a hundred percent rate because:
options: Government refuses to collect at those rates
Revenue is always zero whatever the rate
At zero nothing is levied, and at a hundred percent no one works or declares income to be taxed away entirely

economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.question: Public sector failure occurs when:
options: Government intervention allocates resources LESS efficiently than the market it meant to improve on

economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.question: Which list contains CAUSES of public sector failure?
options: Externalities, public goods and merit goods
Management failure, apathy, bureaucracy, politics overriding economics, and corruption

economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.question: Public sector failure hurts the poor most because:
options: The poor pay the most company tax
Grants are only paid to the wealthy
The wealthy buy private substitutes for failing schools, health and security, while the poor cannot
The poor do not use public services

economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.question: The balanced conclusion the essay requires is:
options: The state should replace all markets
Market failure justifies a public sector and public sector failure disciplines it — the question is which failure is worse in the case at hand, and how each is corrected

economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.question: The bread and the taxi ride are private goods because:
options: The seller can exclude non-payers — you pay, you get

economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.question: The streetlight stays dark without government because:
options: Each neighbour waits for the others to pay, since no one can be excluded from the light once it burns
Streetlights are illegal to buy privately

economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.question: The clinic sits between the bread and the streetlight because:
options: It is non-rivalrous like the streetlight
It cannot charge fees at all
It could charge fees, but vaccination and education carry benefits that spill past the buyer, so the market alone would buy too little

economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.question: The social grant corrects the market's income distribution because:
options: It is a payment for labour supplied
It is a loan that must be repaid
It is a tax on spending
The market pays what labour fetches, not what a family needs — redistribution answers need

economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.question: The bakery stays sharp and the licensing office often does not because:
options: The bakery faces a daily vote — bad bread empties the till tomorrow — while the office's customers cannot go elsewhere and its funding arrives regardless

economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.question: The stepped water tariff — first kilolitres free, then rising blocks — answers the pricing puzzle by:
options: Making basic need free while charging luxury use dearly, so the poor can cook and the reservoir is not emptied on driveways

economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.question: The department cannot bake like the bakery because:
options: No price tells it how many houses or nurses are needed — it must guess through surveys, censuses and politics
Demand for houses does not exist

economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.question: "Serve the social goal and the balance sheet bleeds; serve the balance sheet and the villages go dark" describes:
options: The parastatal tension — a state enterprise pulled between commercial survival and social mandates

economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.question: The main money INTO February's envelope comes from:
options: Income tax on workers, VAT from every till slip, company tax, and duties on fuel, alcohol and tobacco

economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.question: Borrowing every year just to pay salaries and interest is dangerous because:
options: This year's classroom is funded by next year's taxpayer, and interest becomes one of the fastest-growing items in the budget
It strengthens the rand too much
Ports can never be built with loans

economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.question: In the spaza-tax story, pushing the rate past the crest of the hump means:
options: The shop pays double tax happily
Each extra percent collects LESS, as people work less, hide sales or slip into the informal economy

economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.subject: economics
economics.grade12.composition-budgets-an.question: The evaluation mark on the Laffer curve is earned by adding that:
options: The curve proves taxes should be zero
The curve only applies to VAT
Revenue is highest at a hundred percent
Nobody knows precisely where the crest sits — the curve argues for caution, not a precise instruction

economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.subject: economics
economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.question: A business cycle is best defined as:
options: The successive periods of expansion and contraction in real economic activity around a long-term growth trend
Any rise in prices over time
The annual budget cycle of government

economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.subject: economics
economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.question: The four phases of the cycle in correct order, starting from the lowest point, are:

economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.subject: economics
economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.question: The AMPLITUDE of a business cycle is:
options: The time from one peak to the next peak
The slope of the trend line
The vertical distance between the trend line and a peak or trough — a measure of the cycle's intensity
The number of quarters of negative growth

economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.subject: economics
economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.question: A recession is conventionally declared after:
options: One month of falling share prices
A rise in the repo rate
Two consecutive quarters of falling real GDP

economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.subject: economics
economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.question: EXOGENOUS explanations of the cycle locate its causes:
options: Outside the market system — weather, wars, oil shocks, pandemics and policy mistakes
Inside the market system, in confidence and investment swings
Only in the behaviour of trade unions

economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.subject: economics
economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.question: The Keynesian view holds that:
options: Markets are self-correcting and government causes cycles
Markets are inherently unstable — confidence, the multiplier and the accelerator make swings feed themselves, so government must intervene
Cycles are caused only by sunspots and weather
The money supply should grow at a fixed rate

economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.subject: economics
economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.question: Monetarists conclude that the best policy response to cycles is:
options: Stable, predictable policy — because markets self-correct and intervention itself causes the swings

economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.subject: economics
economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.question: Match the cycle to its driver: the Kitchin, Juglar, Kuznets and Kondratieff cycles are driven respectively by:
options: Inventories, machinery investment, building and construction, technological revolutions

economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.subject: economics
economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.question: The SARB's main monetary policy instrument is:
options: The repo rate — the rate at which it lends to commercial banks

economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.subject: economics
economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.question: In the 2020 downswing the SARB cut the repo rate to 3,5 percent. This was:
options: Expansionary monetary policy — cheaper credit to support spending through the trough

economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.subject: economics
economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.question: Automatic stabilisers dampen the cycle because:
options: Parliament votes on them every month
They only operate at the peak
Progressive tax takes less as incomes fall and grants and UIF pay out more as jobs are lost — with no new decision needed
They raise the repo rate automatically

economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.subject: economics
economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.question: A key limit of both monetary and fiscal policy is that:
options: They only work in an upswing
They affect only the foreign sector
They act with lags, so badly timed policy can amplify the very wave it was meant to flatten

economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.subject: economics
economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.question: The new economic paradigm holds that cycles are best smoothed by:
options: Moderate, predictable demand-side policy combined with supply-side measures that raise capacity and efficiency
Maximum government spending at all times

economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.subject: economics
economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.question: Which set contains LEADING indicators?
options: New manufacturing orders, building plans approved, share prices and confidence surveys

economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.subject: economics
economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.question: Unemployment is a LAGGING indicator because:
options: It never changes over the cycle
Firms rehire only once recovery is certain, so it keeps rising after the trough has passed

economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.subject: economics
economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.question: The weakness of EXTRAPOLATION as a forecasting technique is that:
options: It is illegal in national accounting
It assumes the future repeats the past — the assumption that fails exactly at turning points

economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.subject: economics
economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.question: In the tourist town, guesthouses half-empty with nothing getting worse anymore is the:
options: Trough — the lowest point, where activity stops falling

economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.subject: economics
economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.question: During the upswing, the cleaner's new wages are spent at the spaza and those takings are spent again. This climbing-feeding-climbing is:

economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.subject: economics
economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.question: Every room taken, no bricklayer available at any wage, prices creeping up — the town is at:
options: The peak — activity cannot rise further and prices accelerate

economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.subject: economics
economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.question: The wave, the slope and the swing: in the town's story these are respectively:
options: The budget, the repo rate and the deficit
The cycle, the long-term trend, and the amplitude

economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.subject: economics
economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.question: The repo rate works like a thermostat because:
options: Turning it down makes borrowing cheaper and heats up spending; turning it up makes loans pinch and cools spending
It sets the price of petrol
It changes the weather for tourism

economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.subject: economics
economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.question: The rate hikes of 2022 and 2023 were the thermostat turned:
options: Up, to cool spending and slow the climb in prices

economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.subject: economics
economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.question: The waiter who loses his job stops paying income tax and starts drawing UIF. This shows that:
options: The safety net is also a shock absorber — spending falls by less than the wage did, with nobody deciding anything

economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.subject: economics
economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.question: "Neither lever builds a power station" means:
options: Monetary policy is stronger than fiscal policy
Electricity is not part of the economy
Power stations are built by the Reserve Bank
Demand-side tools cannot fix a supply-side constraint — cheap loans and big budgets queue money behind the outage

economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.subject: economics
economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.question: Bookings made months ahead and building plans approved at the municipality are:
options: Leading indicators — actions taken today because of what people expect tomorrow

economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.subject: economics
economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.question: Averaging each month's takings with its neighbours to strip out short-term noise is called:

economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.subject: economics
economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.question: Extrapolation "works right up until the turning point" because:
options: It projects the current path forward, and turning points are precisely where the path changes
It only applies to leading indicators

economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.subject: economics
economics.grade12.features-causes-and-sm.question: "Narrow the amplitude, raise the trend" summarises:
options: The Keynesian rejection of all policy
A plan to abolish business cycles completely
The new paradigm — steady demand-side policy to keep swings small, plus supply-side measures to lift the long-term growth path

economics.grade12.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade12.growth-development-and.question: Economic growth is measured by:
options: The annual percentage change in real GDP — real, so inflation cannot masquerade as progress
The number of new businesses registered

economics.grade12.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade12.growth-development-and.question: With population growing about 1,5 percent a year, South African real GDP growth of 1 percent means:
options: The average person is getting poorer even as the economy grows

economics.grade12.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade12.growth-development-and.question: The three dimensions of the HDI are:
options: A long and healthy life, knowledge, and a decent standard of living

economics.grade12.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade12.growth-development-and.question: "Growth without development" describes:
options: A country whose HDI rises while GDP falls
A country with no natural resources
An economy expanding through capital-intensive exports while employment, schooling and life expectancy stand still — the resource-enclave pattern

economics.grade12.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade12.growth-development-and.question: Demand-side approaches raise growth by:
options: Raising spending — C, I, G and X — and trusting the multiplier to translate it into income and jobs

economics.grade12.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade12.growth-development-and.question: Grants are powerful spending fuel because:
options: They are paid in foreign currency
The poor's high marginal propensity to consume sends almost every grant rand straight into spending

economics.grade12.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade12.growth-development-and.question: The IMPORT wall against South African stimulus is that:
options: A high marginal propensity to import leaks a large slice of any stimulus abroad — the small-multiplier problem

economics.grade12.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade12.growth-development-and.question: The summary evaluation of demand-side measures is that they:
options: Treat symptoms quickly and visibly, but where the binding constraints are on the supply side they buy relief, not transformation

economics.grade12.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade12.growth-development-and.question: Supply-side approaches aim to:
options: Shift the production possibility frontier outward by raising the economy's capacity to produce

economics.grade12.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade12.growth-development-and.question: Infrastructure failure "taxes the whole economy at once" because:
options: Unreliable electricity, ports and rail raise every producer's costs simultaneously

economics.grade12.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade12.growth-development-and.question: The main weaknesses of supply-side measures are that they are:
options: Slow to pay off, socially regressive in the short run, and dependent on the very state capacity whose failures are well known

economics.grade12.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade12.growth-development-and.question: The mature evaluation of the two approaches is:
options: Sequencing and proportion — demand-side protects people through the present while supply-side decides whether the future is bigger; do both in proportion

economics.grade12.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade12.growth-development-and.question: South Africa's growth strategies in correct order are:

economics.grade12.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade12.growth-development-and.question: The honest verdict on South Africa's endeavours is:
options: Every target of every plan was met
Macro stability and the social wage are real achievements, but growth has trailed population and the named constraints — electricity, logistics, skills, state capacity — remain

economics.grade12.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade12.growth-development-and.question: A mechanism that keeps the north-south gap open is:
options: The South's control of world financial institutions
Free technology transfer to the South
Tariff structures that tax processed goods more than raw ones, discouraging southern industrialisation
The North's dependence on southern manufactured exports

economics.grade12.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade12.growth-development-and.question: South Africa "sits astride the line" because it is:
options: Southern in poverty and history yet northern in financial sophistication and industrial base — a dual character

economics.grade12.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade12.growth-development-and.question: The first family — income up, children out of school, winters of coughing — shows:
options: Growth without development — money up, life not

economics.grade12.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade12.growth-development-and.question: "A payslip that grows slower than the family does is a pay cut wearing a smile" is the household version of:
options: Real GDP per capita falling when growth trails population growth

economics.grade12.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade12.growth-development-and.question: The country-scale report card that grades long life, learning and affordable living is:

economics.grade12.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade12.growth-development-and.question: The honest two-fact sentence about South Africa is:
options: High growth and a poor report card
No growth and no development since 1994
The world's best payslip and report card
A payslip that has barely kept up with the family's size, and a report card better than the payslip explains — because grants, clinics and housing did real work

economics.grade12.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade12.growth-development-and.question: "Feeding the fire" stands for:
options: Demand-side policy — money into pockets, spent and re-spent, warmth spreading through the multiplier

economics.grade12.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade12.growth-development-and.question: "Pour money in when the pots are already full and you get higher prices" is the household version of:
options: Stimulus at full capacity multiplying inflation instead of output

economics.grade12.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade12.growth-development-and.question: The stove's slowness is described as "the price of its permanence" because:
options: Schools, skills and infrastructure take years to build but then raise production every day, forever

economics.grade12.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade12.growth-development-and.question: The proportion sentence concludes:
options: Only build the stove, whatever the hunger
Fires and stoves are unrelated to policy
Feed the fire enough to hold everyone through the present, and never stop building the stove

economics.grade12.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade12.growth-development-and.question: The suburb's gate tariff — raw things nearly free, manufactured things taxed — matters because:
options: It discourages the street from ever owning a stove — southern industrialisation is penalised at the gate
It only affects the suburb's own producers
It is set by the street's families

economics.grade12.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade12.growth-development-and.question: "None of this needs a villain" means:
options: The divide persists through structural mechanisms — terms of trade, debt in foreign currency, tariff escalation, brain drain — not personal malice
The suburb secretly plans the street's poverty

economics.grade12.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade12.growth-development-and.question: Evidence that "the story is no longer only the gap" includes:
options: The end of all world trade
The street refusing to trade at all
East Asia's rise, south-south trade and the AfCFTA, and remittances outweighing aid

economics.grade12.growth-development-and.subject: economics
economics.grade12.growth-development-and.question: South Africa as "the corner house" must therefore:
options: Choose the suburb and forget the street
Choose the street and abandon its industry
Wait for the map to redraw itself
Hold both tasks at once — build the stove of growth while keeping the fire of development burning under everyone

economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.subject: economics
economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.question: Which list contains ONLY leading indicators?
options: Building plans passed, job advertisements, new vehicle sales, factory orders
Retail sales, industrial production, real GDP
The repo rate, the prime rate, the Gini coefficient

economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.subject: economics
economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.question: Unemployment is classified as a LAGGING indicator because:
options: It is measured only once a year
Firms retrench late in a downturn and rehire cautiously in a recovery, so jobs move after the cycle turns

economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.subject: economics
economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.question: 'An economy can be large and shrinking, or small and booming' warns against confusing:
options: The LEVEL of GDP with its growth RATE

economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.subject: economics
economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.question: Nominal GDP grew 8% while inflation was 6%. Real growth was about:

economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.subject: economics
economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.question: GDP grows 1% while population grows 1,5%. GDP per capita:
options: Falls — output per person shrinks even as the economy grows

economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.subject: economics
economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.question: The broadest money supply aggregate, tracked by the Reserve Bank, is:
options: M3 — M1's coins, notes and demand deposits plus all shorter and longer-term deposits

economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.subject: economics
economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.question: The terms of trade IMPROVE when:
options: Export prices rise relative to import prices — a national raise earned without producing more

economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.subject: economics
economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.question: The EXPANDED unemployment rate differs from the strict rate by:
options: Adding discouraged work-seekers who have given up searching

economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.subject: economics
economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.question: Life expectancy is called the great summary statistic of development because:
options: It compresses nutrition, healthcare, sanitation and safety into one number
It never changes within a generation

economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.subject: economics
economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.question: The infant mortality rate measures:
options: Deaths before age one per thousand live births — the most sensitive poverty gauge

economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.subject: economics
economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.question: The Human Development Index blends:
options: Life expectancy, education and income per person into a score between 0 and 1

economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.subject: economics
economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.question: South Africa's Gini coefficient of roughly 0,63 to 0,65 indicates:
options: That most income is earned informally
Inequality among the highest ever recorded — 0 means everyone equal, 1 means one person owns everything

economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.subject: economics
economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.question: Purchasing power parity conversion exists because:
options: Market exchange rates understate poor countries — money buys more haircuts, taxi rides and vegetables at home than its dollar value suggests
Rich countries have higher prices for everything everywhere

economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.subject: economics
economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.question: Measured gaps between rich and poor countries tend to OVERSTATE true gaps because:
options: Indicators miss the informal sector, unpaid household work and subsistence farming — all proportionally larger in poorer countries
The World Bank adjusts figures upward

economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.subject: economics
economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.question: The clean one-line separation of the two Bretton Woods institutions:
options: Both lend only to rich countries
The World Bank sets exchange rates; the IMF builds dams
The IMF handles short-term crisis finance and stability; the World Bank funds long-term development projects
The IMF is private; the World Bank is a charity

economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.subject: economics
economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.question: IMF loans are 'both lifelines and lightning rods' because:
options: They carry conditionality — policy changes, often austerity, demanded in exchange for the rescue

economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.subject: economics
economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.question: In the taxi picture, building plans passed are headlights because:
options: Nobody passes a building plan for fun — someone intends to build next year

economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.subject: economics
economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.question: Jobs are the rear-view mirror because a boss:
options: Delays retrenching when times turn bad and delays hiring until sure the recovery is real — so jobs move last

economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.subject: economics
economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.question: 'Rands stretch; kilometres do not' means:
options: Distance is harder to measure than money
Money figures inflate with prices, so real comparison strips inflation out first

economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.subject: economics
economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.question: South Africa's life expectancy story — collapse, then a rise of more than ten years — proves that:
options: Policy shows up in social indicators within a generation, as antiretroviral treatment demonstrated

economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.subject: economics
economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.question: 'Enrolment without learning is a full classroom and an empty gauge' warns that:
options: Attendance figures flatter education unless outcomes — actual learning — are measured too

economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.subject: economics
economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.question: Taps, toilets and electricity are called 'development you can touch' because:
options: Household service access measures whether growth reaches daily life — and post-1994 electrification reached about nine homes in ten
They are leading indicators of GDP

economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.subject: economics
economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.question: The Gini coefficient asks:
options: How much money the country earns
However much money there is, how it is SHARED — from 0, equal, to 1, one person holding everything

economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.subject: economics
economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.question: 'Divide by the passengers' means:
options: Compare living standards per capita — a giant economy can still be poor per person
Divide GDP by the number of provinces

economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.subject: economics
economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.question: PPP repricing can change a country's measured standing by:
options: Doubling or more, because it values income by what it actually buys at home
Making rich countries look poorer than poor ones

economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.subject: economics
economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.question: The paramedic-and-builder pairing is:
options: World Bank for crises; IMF for dams
Both institutions lend only to banks
IMF for balance-of-payments crises with conditions; World Bank for patient development lending — and SA called the paramedic in the pandemic
IMF for private firms; World Bank for governments only

economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.subject: economics
economics.grade12.indicators-and-interna.question: Why does a fast taxi still need its passengers checked?
options: Because GDP can rise while health, education and equality stagnate — growth is not development until it reaches human lives

economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.subject: economics
economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.question: Beneficiation means:
options: Processing raw materials into higher-value products before export — export the bakkie, not the ore
Selling raw materials at world prices

economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.subject: economics
economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.question: A vehicle plant's BACKWARD linkages are:
options: The dealerships and mechanics that sell and service its vehicles
The suppliers it pulls into existence — component makers, transporters, toolmakers
Its debts to the development bank

economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.subject: economics
economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.question: Why does a commodity-exporting economy need industrial diversification for STABILITY?
options: Its earnings ride the roller-coaster of world commodity prices, while a diversified base spreads risk across many products and markets

economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.subject: economics
economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.question: The infant-industry caution warns that:
options: New industries should never be supported
Support without a finish line breeds industries that stay comfortable instead of becoming competitive, at consumers' expense

economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.subject: economics
economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.question: South Africa's rolling industrial policy blueprints, under the 2007 framework, are the:
options: Industrial Policy Action Plans — the IPAPs, run by the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition

economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.subject: economics
economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.question: The APDP supports the automotive industry by:
options: Rewarding local production and investment with import-duty credits and investment allowances

economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.subject: economics
economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.question: The Industrial Development Corporation's role is to:
options: Set the repo rate for industry
Finance industrial projects that commercial banks find too slow or too risky

economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.subject: economics
economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.question: Localisation through designated procurement means:
options: Factories may only hire local workers
Firms must relocate to rural areas
State entities must buy specified products — buses, rail stock, uniforms — from local producers, guaranteeing factories a market

economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.subject: economics
economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.question: Left to the market, industry clusters in a few regions because:
options: Firms settle where suppliers, customers, ports and skills already are
Workers refuse to live outside Gauteng

economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.subject: economics
economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.question: Apartheid's homeland decentralisation policy mostly failed because:
options: Incentives could not outweigh the absence of infrastructure, markets and skills — factories died when subsidies stopped

economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.subject: economics
economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.question: The Maputo Development Corridor is:
options: A fenced industrial park in Gauteng
An SDI linking Gauteng's industry to Maputo's port through N4 road, rail and border upgrades in public-private partnership
A shipping route between Durban and Cape Town

economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.subject: economics
economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.question: Which is a genuine part of the SEZ incentive package under the 2014 Act?
options: A reduced corporate tax rate of 15 percent, building allowances, employment tax incentives and duty-free inputs for export production

economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.subject: economics
economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.question: The international best-practice recipe for industrial policy ties support to:
options: Export performance, keeps it temporary and conditional, and invests in skills and infrastructure alongside
Permanent protection of all local firms

economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.subject: economics
economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.question: The single most damning aggregate fact in evaluating SA industrial policy is that:
options: Manufacturing's share of GDP has drifted down from over 19 percent toward 12 to 13 percent — deindustrialisation

economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.subject: economics
economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.question: The binding-constraints test argues that:
options: Incentives should be doubled every year
Fixing electricity, ports, rail and skills may matter more than any subsidy, because incentives cannot compensate for failing networks

economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.subject: economics
economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.question: 'Rands per sustainable job' is a criterion because:
options: Jobs cannot be counted any other way
It is required by the Constitution
Incentives spend public money, and a zone needing permanent subsidy repeats the homeland mistake in modern clothing

economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.subject: economics
economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.question: The bakkie earns far more than the bag of ore because:
options: Its price contains the wages, profits and taxes of every making step performed at home

economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.subject: economics
economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.question: Hundreds of businesses 'hang off one assembly line' because:
options: Suppliers stand behind the plant and dealers and mechanics stand in front of it — the linkage web
Assembly lines are cheap to build

economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.subject: economics
economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.question: Support for an industry 'must have a finish line' because:
options: An industry surviving only on protection is a permanent tax on everyone else, paid in higher prices

economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.subject: economics
economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.question: The Coega package offers investors:
options: A ready-built zone with port, roads, power and water, plus 15 percent company tax, building help, hiring tax breaks and duty-free inputs for exporters
Free labour and free land forever
A monopoly on the South African market

economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.subject: economics
economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.question: A corridor differs from a zone because it:
options: Wakes up a whole line of towns along a route, rather than one fenced site

economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.subject: economics
economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.question: The homeland-factories lesson in one sentence:
options: You can pay a factory to arrive anywhere, but it only stays where business actually works

economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.subject: economics
economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.question: Zones fail when they are:
options: Only a fence and a tax break in an empty field, without transport, power and skills fixed underneath

economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.subject: economics
economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.question: A balanced evaluation of SA industrial strategy opens by:
options: Stating the test — help tied to exports, temporary, standing on working infrastructure and skills

economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.subject: economics
economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.question: Which pairing correctly matches a named WIN with a named FAILURE?
options: The car programme failed; clothing thrived
The car programme and Coega's tenants as wins; collapsed clothing employment and empty-shed zones as failures
The Maputo Corridor failed; homeland factories thrived
Deindustrialisation as a win; vehicle exports as a failure

economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.subject: economics
economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.question: The 'real bottleneck' move earns top marks because it argues:
options: That more sweeteners are always the answer
That incentives cannot outweigh power cuts, broken rail, queuing ports and scarce skills — so fixing foundations may beat any subsidy

economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.subject: economics
economics.grade12.industrial-and-regiona.question: A defensible one-sentence verdict on SA's strategy is:
options: Everything failed and should be scrapped
Everything worked and needs no change
No verdict is possible in economics
The direction is right and the flagships earn their keep, but the strategy underperforms while the foundations crumble

economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..subject: economics
economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..question: Inflation is best defined as:
options: A sustained and significant increase in the GENERAL price level over time
Any increase in the price of bread
A once-off rise in prices after a VAT increase
A fall in the value of the rand against the dollar

economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..subject: economics
economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..question: Inflation falls from 7% to 5%. This is called:
options: Disinflation — prices still rising, but more slowly

economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..subject: economics
economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..question: The weights in the CPI basket are determined by:
options: The prices charged by the largest retailers
Household surveys of what South Africans actually spend their money on
Parliament, when it passes the budget

economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..subject: economics
economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..question: The difference between the CPI and the PPI is that:
options: The PPI includes services and the CPI does not
The CPI is measured yearly and the PPI monthly
The PPI is always higher than the CPI
The CPI measures the cost of living at the till, while the PPI measures the cost of production at the factory gate

economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..subject: economics
economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..question: The base-year trolley cost R4 000; the same trolley now costs R4 480. The index now stands at:

economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..subject: economics
economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..question: The CPI moves from 112,0 to 118,7 over a year. The inflation rate is:
options: About 6,0% — the 6,7-point change divided by the OLD index of 112,0, times 100

economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..subject: economics
economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..question: A basket has food (weight 50%, up 10%), transport (30%, up 5%) and school costs (20%, up 20%). Weighted inflation is:

economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..subject: economics
economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..question: A wage rises 4% in a year when inflation is 6%. In real terms the wage has:
options: Fallen by roughly 2% — the rand figures grew, but the trolley they can fill shrank

economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..subject: economics
economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..question: Demand-pull inflation occurs when:
options: Total spending grows faster than the economy's capacity to produce — too much money chasing too few goods
Production costs rise and are passed on to consumers
The government fixes prices by law

economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..subject: economics
economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..question: Which list contains ONLY cost-push causes?
options: Cheap credit, consumer booms, export surges
A weaker rand raising import costs, electricity tariff hikes, wage settlements above productivity
Government deficits, investment booms, rising incomes
Falling interest rates and rising grants

economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..subject: economics
economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..question: In the curve story, cost-push inflation is shown by:
options: Aggregate demand shifting right — prices up, output up
Aggregate demand shifting left — prices down
Aggregate supply shifting left — prices up, output DOWN

economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..subject: economics
economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..question: Stagflation is the combination of:
options: Rising prices together with falling output and rising unemployment

economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..subject: economics
economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..question: Inflation redistributes wealth from:
options: Creditors to debtors — loans are repaid in shrunken rands

economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..subject: economics
economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..question: A saver earns 5% interest while inflation runs at 6%. The real interest rate is:
options: Minus 1% — the nominal rate minus the inflation rate

economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..subject: economics
economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..question: South Africa's inflation-targeting framework requires the Reserve Bank to keep CPI inflation:
options: Inside a band of 3 to 6 percent, using the repo rate as its main instrument
Equal to the growth rate of GDP

economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..subject: economics
economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..question: Why does raising the repo rate work poorly against cost-push inflation?
options: Because banks ignore the repo rate
Because it makes the rand weaker
Because cost-push inflation is not real inflation
Because higher interest rates cannot lower production costs — they only suppress demand, at the price of output and jobs

economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..subject: economics
economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..question: The CPI 'trolley' is filled according to:
options: What surveys show households actually buy, with bigger spending items taking more space

economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..subject: economics
economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..question: An index reading of 112 means:
options: What cost R100 in the base year now costs R112

economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..subject: economics
economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..question: Your family's costs rose faster than the official inflation rate. This is possible because:
options: Statistics South Africa only prices luxury goods
The official rate is set by the shops
The official trolley is an average basket, and no household's spending matches the average exactly
Inflation is measured only once a decade

economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..subject: economics
economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..question: The tell-tale sign of demand-pull inflation is:
options: Shops busy, goods selling out, order books full — many hands reaching for few goods

economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..subject: economics
economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..question: A drought raises maize prices and electricity tariffs jump. Prices rise while shops stay quiet. This is:
options: Cost-push inflation — costs pushing prices up from behind, even though customers are not spending more

economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..subject: economics
economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..question: Pointing the repo-rate 'hose' at a cost-push fire mainly:
options: Suppresses spending and jobs while the cost pressure remains

economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..subject: economics
economics.grade12.inflation-and-the-cpi..question: Why must an essay say WHICH type of inflation is burning before recommending policy?
options: Because both types have the same cure
